We present the clinical case of a 20-year-old male patient who presented 
recurrent pneumothorax on 5 occasions
evidence.explanation: Recurrent pneumothorax as the presenting feature of a molecularly confirmed CHDSKM patient.

evidence.snippet: Phenotypes such as skeletal malformations, aortic root dilatation and pneumothorax point towards an overlap with genetic connective tissue disorders
evidence.explanation: Places pneumothorax within the connective-tissue overlap of the syndrome.

steps/28.description: Spontaneous pneumothorax, sometimes recurrent, is an uncommon but diagnostically important manifestation: it is one of the features that places CHDSKM in the differential of heritable connective-tissue disease, and in at least one patient recurrent pneumothorax was the presenting complaint that led to the molecular diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: These results are consistent with gain of ABL1 tyrosine kinase activity due to loss of auto-inhibition by myristoyl binding.
evidence.explanation: States the causal link itself - loss of autoinhibition producing the gain of kinase activity - rather than either endpoint alone.

edges/1.description: Loss of autoinhibition is the direct cause of the elevated kinase activity, not merely a correlate: the same variants that disrupt the regulatory elements are the ones that raise catalytic output.

evidence.snippet: Phosphorylation of ABL1-Tyr245 and STAT5B were substantially increased in lysates transfected with the c.1066G > A p.(Ala356Thr) construct
evidence.explanation: Directly couples the variant kinase to increased substrate phosphorylation in the same experiment.

evidence.snippet: Treatment with 1 µM imatinib results in complete loss of phosphorylation activity.
evidence.explanation: Pharmacological interruption of the kinase abolishes the downstream phosphorylation, supporting the direction of this edge.

edges/2.description: The elevated kinase activity is measured as, and therefore directly produces, increased phosphorylation of ABL1 substrates. The edge is reversible in vitro: inhibiting the kinase removes the substrate phosphorylation.

edges/7.description: Summary edge: the structural congenital heart disease of CHDSKM is the clinical manifestation of this disrupted septation and outflow tract development.

edges/8.description: Failed atrial septation presents clinically as the atrial septal defect.

edges/9.description: Failed ventricular septation presents clinically as the ventricular septal defect.

edges/10.description: Failure of ductal closure is part of the outflow-tract arm of the disrupted cardiac development.

edges/11.description: Supravalvular pulmonary stenosis is the right-outflow-tract lesion of the disrupted outflow tract development.

edges/13.description: Summary edge: the digital anomalies are the most consistent direct manifestation of the disrupted skeletal morphogenesis.

edges/14.description: Fixed interphalangeal flexion deformity, the commonest single digital manifestation of the disrupted skeletal morphogenesis.

edges/15.description: Finger contractures are a direct digital manifestation of the disrupted skeletal morphogenesis.

edges/16.description: Fifth-finger incurving is a direct digital manifestation of the disrupted skeletal morphogenesis.

edges/17.description: Cutaneous 2-3 toe syndactyly is a direct digital manifestation of the disrupted skeletal morphogenesis.

edges/18.description: Long slender digits, the marfanoid digital manifestation of the disrupted skeletal and connective tissue development.

edges/19.description: Axial-skeleton manifestation of the disrupted skeletal morphogenesis.

edges/20.description: Thoracic-cage manifestation of the disrupted skeletal morphogenesis.

edges/21.description: The high-arched palate belongs to the marfanoid connective-tissue dimension of the disrupted skeletal morphogenesis described on this node.

edges/22.description: Joint laxity is a manifestation of the connective-tissue dimension of this node.

edges/23.description: Thin skin is a manifestation of the connective-tissue dimension of this node.

edges/24.description: Pneumothorax is grouped by the sources with the connective-tissue overlap phenotypes; the presumed route (pleural or bleb fragility on a weakened connective-tissue background, as in other heritable connective-tissue disorders) has not been demonstrated in CHDSKM, hence the indirect typing.

edges/25.description: Summary edge: the aortic root dilatation phenotype is the echocardiographic observation of this tissue-level process, and is what the recommended serial surveillance monitors.

edges/26.description: The prenatal component of the growth impairment presents as intrauterine growth restriction.

edges/27.description: The postnatal component of the growth impairment presents as failure to thrive with feeding difficulty.

edges/28.description: Short stature is the majority adult outcome of the growth impairment; expressivity is variable and a minority of adults are tall, so the edge describes the usual, not universal, endpoint.

evidence.snippet:
The variant c.734A>G (p.Tyr245Cys) was found to occur de novo or 
cosegregate with disease in five individuals (families 1-3).
evidence.explanation: Identifies the recurrent founding ABL1 allele for CHDSKM.

evidence.snippet:
Here, we describe a series of 
six new unrelated individuals with heterozygous missense variants in ABL1 
(including four novel variants) identified via whole exome sequencing.
evidence.explanation: Expands the allelic series with four additional novel missense variants.

evidence.snippet:
we describe three de novo missense variants, c.407C>T (p.Thr136Met), 
c.746C>T (p.Pro249Leu), and c.1573G>A (p.Val525Met), and one recurrent variant, 
c.1066G>A (p.Ala356Thr), in six patients
evidence.explanation: Further extends the pathogenic ABL1 missense allele spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Heterozygotes of both strains are largely unaffected, suggesting that ABL1 does not display haploinsufficiency, and supporting the possibility that the human germline missense variants act through a gain of function.
evidence.explanation: Mouse heterozygous null data argue against haploinsufficiency and for a gain-of-function disease mechanism in the human syndrome.

genes/0.notes: ABL1 (9q34.12) encodes a ubiquitously expressed non-receptor tyrosine kinase. CHDSKM alleles are heterozygous germline missense substitutions annotated against the isoform 1b transcript NM_007313.2. They are not haploinsufficiency alleles: mouse heterozygotes for Abl1 null alleles are largely unaffected, and the human alleles increase rather than decrease kinase output. Reported disease alleles include p.Val244Ala, p.Tyr245Cys, p.Gln300Glu, p.Ala356Thr, p.Ala452Thr, p.Ile508Leu, p.Val525Ala, and p.Glu528Lys, plus p.Thr136Met, p.Pro249Leu, p.Val525Met, and p.Trp67Arg. The recurrent alleles p.Tyr245Cys and p.Ala356Thr account for a disproportionate share of reported patients. Note that only a subset of these alleles has been localised to a named regulatory element: the myristoyl-pocket cluster (Ala356, Ala452, Val525, Glu528) and the SH2-kinase linker (Val244, Tyr245) are mapped, whereas p.Trp67Arg, p.Thr136Met, p.Pro249Leu, p.Gln300Glu, and p.Ile508Leu are reported without a domain assignment beyond, for p.Ile508Leu, the kinase domain.

evidence.snippet: The CHD included atrial/ventricular septal defects and in older individuals aortic root dilation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the repairable lesion set that this treatment addresses. No CHDSKM-specific surgical series or outcome data exist, so this is indication evidence only and supports no efficacy claim; the lesions are managed under general congenital heart disease practice.

treatments/0.description: Defect-specific management of septal defects, patent ductus arteriosus, and outflow tract lesions by paediatric or adult congenital cardiology, following standard congenital heart disease practice. There is no CHDSKM-specific cardiac surgical protocol; the lesions are managed on their own merits.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, assessment of the aortic root diameter at the time of diagnosis may also be appropriate in individuals found to have pathogenic ABL1 variants.
evidence.explanation: Direct expert recommendation for baseline aortic root assessment.

evidence.snippet: a precautionary approach of ongoing aortic root screening similar to that used for Marfan syndrome may be appropriate until such time as more accurate natural history data are available
evidence.explanation: States the Marfan-modelled, explicitly precautionary basis for serial surveillance.

evidence.snippet:
lend strength to previous calls for close surveillance of the aortic 
root from a young age in CHDSKM
evidence.explanation: Independent case reinforcing early and close aortic root surveillance.

treatments/1.description: Baseline measurement of the aortic root diameter at diagnosis and ongoing serial imaging, explicitly modelled on Marfan syndrome surveillance. The expert recommendation is explicitly precautionary: the true risk of aneurysm and dissection in CHDSKM is unknown, and as of the 2021 pooled series no patient had been reported to require surgical intervention for rapid progressive dilatation. A 2023 case has since documented severe and rapidly progressive dilatation, which strengthens rather than weakens the case for surveillance; the recommendation stands until natural-history data become available.

evidence.snippet: The high prevalence of hearing impairment makes audiological assessment advisable.
evidence.explanation: Direct expert recommendation for audiological assessment in CHDSKM.

treatments/2.description: Formal audiology at diagnosis and thereafter, with hearing aids or ENT intervention as indicated. The rationale is the high frequency of conductive and mixed hearing impairment in the syndrome, which was under-recognised in the original description. No NCIT clinical-action term for audiological assessment is reachable from NCIT:C25218, so this treatment carries a free-text preferred_term only.

evidence.snippet: Most individuals had failure to thrive during infancy and early childhood
evidence.explanation: Establishes the clinical need being addressed; no CHDSKM-specific nutritional intervention study exists, so this is indication evidence only.

treatments/3.description: Nutritional and feeding management during infancy and early childhood, addressing the feeding difficulties and growth failure that affect most patients. Supportive rather than disease-modifying.

evidence.snippet: ScoliosisYes (surgical intervention)
evidence.explanation: Table entry recording surgical intervention for scoliosis in a CHDSKM patient; establishes the practice, not an efficacy claim.

treatments/4.description: Spinal surveillance with bracing or surgical correction for progressive scoliosis, and physiotherapy, occupational therapy, or surgery for finger contractures, camptodactyly, and foot deformity. At least one reported patient required surgical intervention for scoliosis.

evidence.snippet: failure to thrive (14/18), developmental delay (11/18), IUGR (10/18)
evidence.explanation: Establishes the developmental-delay burden that this supportive care addresses; indication evidence only, with no efficacy claim.

treatments/5.description: Physical, occupational, and speech and language therapy with developmental paediatric follow-up, indicated by the developmental delay present in a majority of reported patients and by the hand-function consequences of camptodactyly and finger contractures. Supportive; there is no CHDSKM-specific rehabilitation protocol or outcome study.

evidence.snippet: Finally, as expected, imatinib abolished phosphorylation of ABL1-Tyr245 and STAT5B in all of the constructs
evidence.explanation: In vitro pharmacological tractability only; there is no clinical evidence of benefit in CHDSKM.

evidence.snippet: While imatinib is used to treat paediatric CML cases, it is expected to be teratogenic in pregnancy. Further work is therefore required to ascertain whether therapeutic scope exists for use of imatinib or similar TKIs in this condition.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own caveat, stated as expert discussion rather than as a reported observation: teratogenicity risk and absence of evidence for therapeutic scope in this condition.

evidence.snippet: TKIs may potentially in some way be therapeutically beneficial for the ABL1 developmental syndrome or its complications, for example in limiting aortic root dilatation or reducing the tendency for dilatation to occur.
evidence.explanation: The therapeutic hypothesis the same authors advance, recorded alongside their cautions so the entry reflects both halves of the source argument.

evidence.snippet: severe congenital malformations have been reported in fetuses exposed to imatinib, a selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor drug
evidence.explanation: Documents the fetal malformation signal that makes developmental use of this drug class hazardous; note the same paragraph states that no definitive conclusion about imatinib teratogenicity can be drawn from the small, confounded case set.

evidence.snippet:
In contrast, the 
allosteric inhibitor asciminib strongly reduces Abl's activity by fixating the 
αI-helix and reducing the force onto the SH2 domain.
evidence.explanation: Supports the mechanistic distinction between allosteric and type II ATP-site inhibition that complicates drug selection in this syndrome.

treatments/6.description: NOT an established treatment. Imatinib abolishes the excess phosphorylation of mutant ABL1 constructs in vitro, which makes the gain-of-function mechanism pharmacologically tractable in principle and is the sole basis for interest in ABL-directed tyrosine kinase inhibitors here. The authors of that work do advance a therapeutic hypothesis: because the germline alleles functionally mimic the loss of the ABL1 N-terminus in BCR-ABL, they expect TKIs effective against BCR-ABL to be similarly effective against the variant proteins, and they raise limiting aortic root dilatation as a candidate indication. Three considerations nevertheless weigh against clinical use outside a rigorously justified research protocol. First, the malformations arise during embryofetal development, so any meaningful effect would require treatment from a very early age and lifelong exposure. Second, imatinib is expected to be teratogenic in pregnancy, and severe congenital malformations have been reported in fetuses exposed to it - though the original authors caution that no definitive conclusion about imatinib teratogenicity can be drawn from the small number of cases, several of which also involved exposure to other teratogens such as warfarin or hydroxyurea. Third, structural work shows that type II ATP-site inhibitors such as imatinib promote disassembly of the very regulatory core whose disassembly drives the disease, whereas the allosteric myristoyl-pocket inhibitor asciminib stabilises the alpha-I helix instead - so the two inhibitor classes are not interchangeable and leukaemia dosing cannot simply be transplanted into a developmental syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Malignancies have not been detected in any of the affected individuals with ABL1 germline variants, but as they cause increased phosphorylation and possibly increased kinase activity of this proto-oncogene, it may be prudent to perform systematic clinical screening for ABL1-associated cancers in the newly identified individuals.
evidence.explanation: The recommendation and its explicitly prudential, unvalidated basis, both stated in the same sentence; no risk estimate, modality, or interval is given.

treatments/7.description: Systematic clinical screening for ABL1-associated cancers, recommended by the authors of the original description on the precautionary grounds that the germline alleles increase the activity of a proto-oncogene. This is a prudential recommendation, not an evidence-based protocol: no malignancy has been reported in any CHDSKM patient, no screening modality or interval has been specified or validated, and the lifetime risk is unquantified. The corresponding evidence gap is tracked in the chdskm_malignancy_risk discussion.

evidence.snippet: expanding the phenotypic spectrum of CHDSKM to include hearing impairment, lipodystrophy-like features, renal hypoplasia, and distinct ocular abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Renal hypoplasia in the documented spectrum is the indication for baseline renal imaging.

treatments/8.description: Renal ultrasound at diagnosis, indicated by the renal hypoplasia added to the CHDSKM spectrum by the expanded series and by the unilateral renal agenesis recorded in the case-series table. Detection-oriented; no CHDSKM-specific screening interval has been defined.

evidence.snippet: expanding the phenotypic spectrum of CHDSKM to include hearing impairment, lipodystrophy-like features, renal hypoplasia, and distinct ocular abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Distinct ocular abnormalities in the documented spectrum are the indication for baseline eye examination.

treatments/9.description: Eye examination at diagnosis, indicated by the distinct ocular abnormalities added to the CHDSKM spectrum by the expanded series. The source does not enumerate the findings in its abstract, so this is a detection-oriented baseline rather than a search for a specified lesion.

evidence.snippet: In family 3, p.Tyr245Cys was found to be inherited from the similarly affected father.
evidence.explanation: Documented parent-to-child transmission establishes the recurrence risk that genetic counseling addresses.

treatments/10.description: Counseling for the recurrence risk from an affected heterozygous parent, with cascade testing of at-risk relatives once a familial variant is identified. Because the condition is autosomal dominant, each pregnancy of an affected heterozygous parent carries a one-in-two transmission risk; the documented father-to-child and mother-to-child transmissions of p.Tyr245Cys make this a real rather than theoretical counseling scenario. Counseling must convey that expressivity is variable, so severity in an affected child cannot be predicted from the parent's phenotype, and that most probands to date have carried de novo variants. Once a familial variant is known, prenatal diagnosis and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disease are technically available reproductive options.

evidence.snippet: AXIN1 and ATRX may be important in elucidating the mechanisms of other phenotypes, such as finger contracture and failure to thrive. Verification of these hypotheses would lead to further understanding of the pathophysiology and the development of treatment methods.
evidence.explanation: The authors explicitly frame the effector assignments as unverified hypotheses requiring further work.

open_questions/0.rationale: Steps 1 to 3 of the causal chain - autoinhibition loss, kinase hyperactivity, increased substrate phosphorylation - are experimentally solid and independently replicated. The step from generalised phosphotyrosine excess to a specific, reproducible malformation pattern is entirely inferential. The only concrete effector nominations come from a single phosphoproteomic experiment in a transfected cell line (UFD1, AXIN1, ATRX), and even the cell types involved - cardiomyocytes, endocardial and valvular interstitial cells, cardiac neural crest derivatives, chondrocytes, craniofacial mesenchyme - remain plausible candidates rather than demonstrated targets. This is why the pathophysiology edges leading out of the phosphorylation node are typed INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES and why no cell types are asserted on the cardiac node.

evidence.snippet: Abl1 knockout mice have growth delay, cardiac hyperplasia and osteoporosis
evidence.explanation: Describes the loss-of-function mouse phenotype available as a model.

evidence.snippet: We re-evaluated the ventricular wall thickness of our patients and confirmed that there is no cardiac hyperplasia
evidence.explanation: Explicitly documents that the mouse cardiac phenotype is not reproduced in human patients - the core of the model mismatch.

open_questions/1.rationale: Every published Abl1 mouse model is a null or truncation allele. Their phenotypes - growth delay, cardiac hyperplasia, osteoporosis, lymphopenia, perinatal lethality - establish that ABL1 matters in development but point in the opposite functional direction from the human disease. The mismatch is not incidental: the original authors specifically re-examined ventricular wall thickness in their patients and confirmed the absence of the cardiac hyperplasia seen in the knockout mice, attributing the difference to increased versus abolished kinase activity. Mouse heterozygotes are largely unaffected, so there is no dosage model either. No knock-in model of a recurrent human CHDSKM allele has been reported.

evidence.snippet: No patients with the ABL1 skeletal and cardiac malformation syndrome described here or elsewhere are reported to have haematological malignancy, but longitudinal follow up of these patients will be required to better determine this.
evidence.explanation: States both the absence of observed malignancy and the insufficiency of current follow-up.

evidence.snippet: Malignancies have not been detected in any of the affected individuals with ABL1 germline variants, but as they cause increased phosphorylation and possibly increased kinase activity of this proto-oncogene, it may be prudent to perform systematic clinical screening for ABL1-associated cancers in the newly identified individuals.
evidence.explanation: The original authors' recommendation for cancer screening in the face of unquantified risk.

open_questions/2.rationale: ABL1 is a proto-oncogene and its constitutive activation in the somatic BCR::ABL1 fusion drives chronic myeloid leukaemia, so a germline activating allele raises an obvious question. No malignancy has been reported in any CHDSKM patient, but the total described cohort is very small and mostly young, so absence of events is weak evidence of absence of risk. There is a mechanistic argument for reassurance - disruption of myristoyl binding alone may not activate ABL1 enough to drive malignancy because two other autoinhibitory linchpins remain intact, whereas BCR::ABL1 loses both the myristoyl group and the N-terminal brace - but this is reasoning, not data. Notably, the authors of the largest functional series report that none of the activating germline variants they describe has been associated with somatic tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance in leukaemia - though one residue, Ala452, is shared between the germline and somatic settings, so the separation is not absolute.

evidence.snippet: thereby expanding the phenotypic spectrum of CHDSKM to include hearing impairment, lipodystrophy-like features, renal hypoplasia, and distinct ocular abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: The expansion series documents these manifestations as clinical observations only, with no mechanistic account, which is the gap this discussion records.

open_questions/3.rationale: The pathophysiology of this entry reaches the cardiac, skeletal, connective-tissue, aortic, and growth phenotypes through tissue-level developmental nodes, but no comparable node exists for the craniofacial, sensory, neurodevelopmental, adipose, renal, genital, or gastrointestinal manifestations. The literature documents these features - several were added to the spectrum only by the 2020 expansion series and the 2021 pooled review - without proposing any mechanism for them beyond the generic observation that ABL1 is ubiquitously expressed; even candidate cell lineages (craniofacial mesenchyme, otic and ocular primordia, neural progenitors, metanephric mesenchyme) are unnamed in the CHDSKM sources. Wiring these phenotypes to the existing substrate-phosphorylation node would assert a specificity the sources do not contain, so they are left causally unexplained until lineage-level evidence exists; the proposed experiments under chdskm_lineage_route_to_malformation would bear on this gap as well.

evidence.snippet: Smoking (odds ratio 2.87 for current vs never, PAR 35.7% for current and former vs never)
evidence.explanation: INTERHEART, a standardised case-control study of acute myocardial infarction across 52 countries with 15152 cases and 14820 controls. Establishes smoking as one of the largest modifiable contributors to population attributable risk.

evidence.snippet: risk increased by 5.6% for every additional cigarette smoked
evidence.explanation: The tobacco-specific INTERHEART analysis. Quoted for the dose-response relationship, which is the part of the note the odds ratio alone does not establish.

evidence.snippet: Meta-regression suggested that greater reductions in saturated fat (reflected in greater reductions in serum cholesterol) resulted in greater reductions in risk of CVD events, explaining most heterogeneity between trials
evidence.explanation: Cochrane review of 15 randomised controlled trials with about 59000 participants. Note this source qualifies the original note rather than simply confirming it: the same abstract reports only small reductions in LDL cholesterol from reducing saturated fat, so LDL elevation is a weaker claim than the cardiovascular event effect, and the note was rewritten accordingly.

evidence.snippet: regular physical activity (0.86, PAR 12.2%)
evidence.explanation: INTERHEART reports regular physical activity as protective against myocardial infarction with a population attributable risk of 12.2 percent for its absence, which is the evidence that inactivity is a risk factor for this disease.

evidence.snippet: for sedentary behavior, represented by screen time > 2 hours/day, a significant association was not identified
evidence.explanation: Cited as a caveat, not support. This meta-analysis of eighteen studies found low physical activity significantly associated with metabolic syndrome, but sedentary behaviour measured as screen time was NOT significantly associated overall - only on weekends in subgroup analysis. It is an adolescent population, so it does not settle the question in adults, but it is enough to show the metabolic-syndrome mechanism should not be stated flatly.

evidence.snippet: abdominal obesity (1.12 for top vs lowest tertile and 1.62 for middle vs lowest tertile, PAR 20.1% for top two tertiles vs lowest tertile)
evidence.explanation: INTERHEART. Note the measure is abdominal obesity by waist/hip ratio rather than body mass index, which is a more specific claim than the entry name suggests.

evidence.snippet: CD36 + positive ECs exhibited significant senescence phenotypes following disturbed flow stimulation.
evidence.explanation: Supports disturbed-flow-associated endothelial senescence as one component of endothelial dysfunction. It does not directly measure nitric-oxide biosynthesis and comes from a mouse carotid model, so it is not treated as direct coronary or nitric-oxide evidence.

evidence.snippet: Atherosclerosis tends to occur in regions of disturbed blood flow. This study explored how disturbed flow aggravates atherosclerosis using single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) datasets from mouse carotid arteries under disturbed flow and human carotid artery plaques.
evidence.explanation: Supports disturbed flow as a regional context for atherosclerosis and endothelial dysfunction. It does not directly establish reduced nitric-oxide biosynthesis or a coronary-specific effect.

steps/4.description: At atherosclerosis-prone arterial sites, disturbed flow is associated with endothelial stress and senescence, while reduced endothelial nitric-oxide biosynthesis represents the vasomotor dysfunction that impairs dilation. This nonconforming coronary endothelial-function branch is modeled separately from the conserved subendothelial apoB-retention trigger. The cited disturbed-flow evidence derives from mouse carotid arteries and human carotid plaques, so its transfer to coronary endothelial dysfunction is explicitly partial.

evidence.snippet: infiltration and retention of apoB containing lipoproteins in the artery wall is a critical initiating event that sparks an inflammatory response and promotes the development of atherosclerosis.
evidence.explanation: Establishes arterial-wall apoB retention as the initiating event; coronary arterial intima is the disease-specific location represented here.

steps/5.description: In the coronary arterial intima, endothelial injury and dysfunction permit infiltration and retention of apoB-containing lipoproteins in the subendothelial space. Retained and modified lipoproteins initiate local inflammation and monocyte recruitment, providing the coronary trigger for atheroma formation.

evidence.snippet: Internalization of the apoB containing lipoproteins by macrophages promotes foam cell formation, which is the hallmark of the fatty streak phase of atherosclerosis.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports macrophage uptake of apoB lipoproteins and foam-cell formation in the fatty streak.

evidence.snippet: Macrophage inflammation results in enhanced oxidative stress and cytokine/chemokine secretion, causing more LDL/remnant oxidation, endothelial cell activation, monocyte recruitment, and foam cell formation.
evidence.explanation: Documents the macrophage inflammatory loop that amplifies foam-cell formation.

steps/6.description: In the coronary intima, recruited monocytes become macrophages and internalize retained apoB-containing lipoproteins, forming lipid-laden foam cells. Their inflammatory feed-forward loop promotes further lipoprotein oxidation, endothelial activation, monocyte recruitment, and foam-cell formation.

evidence.snippet: We examine the cellular and molecular processes that drive the formation of calcified plaques, highlighting the roles of inflammation, lipid accumulation, and smooth muscle cell proliferation.
evidence.explanation: Supports lipid accumulation, inflammation, and smooth-muscle-cell proliferation as contributors to coronary plaque formation. It does not by itself establish the specific phenotypic-switching or matrix-assembly sequence represented by this node.

evidence.snippet: vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching through transdifferentiation and stem/progenitor cell activation resulting in the promotion of inflammation, calcification, and secretion of extracellular matrix, altering fibrous cap structure, and necrotic core growth.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports smooth-muscle-cell phenotypic switching and extracellular-matrix secretion in plaque assembly.

steps/7.description: In the inflamed coronary intima, vascular smooth muscle cells switch to a synthetic, migratory phenotype, proliferate, and organize extracellular matrix to build the fibrofatty plaque and its fibrous cap. This is the atomic smooth-muscle-cell and matrix assembly step of coronary atheroma formation.

evidence.snippet: the local arterial microenvironment of a stable atheroma promotes destabilizing conditions that result in the transition to an unstable atheroma.
evidence.explanation: Human histopathology and vascular-imaging evidence supports transition of a stable mature atheroma to an unstable lesion; coronary artery is the disease-specific location substituted here.

evidence.snippet: Advanced stages of atherosclerosis progression and symptomatic carotid plaques were largely characterized by 3 smooth muscle cells (SMCs), and 3 macrophage subtype clusters with extracellular matrix organization/osteogenic (SMC), and M1-type proinflammatory/Trem2-high lipid-associated (macrophage) phenotypes.
evidence.explanation: Supports the smooth-muscle-cell, extracellular-matrix, and lipid-associated macrophage composition of advanced human atherosclerotic plaque. The tissue studied was carotid plaque, so this is partial support for conserved advanced-atheroma biology rather than direct coronary evidence.

evidence.snippet: Notable increases in VEGFA+ macrophages were discovered in the disturbed flow stimulation group, displaying a pronounced M1 pro-inflammatory phenotype associated with the severity of atherosclerosis and plaque stability.
evidence.explanation: Supports an inflammatory macrophage phenotype associated with plaque severity and stability, not rupture or thrombosis. The disturbed-flow comparison is from a mouse carotid model, so support for coronary advanced atheroma is partial.

evidence.snippet: By identifying and integrating the most gene-rich single-cell subclusters of atherosclerosis to date with a coronary artery disease framework of GRNs, GRN39 was identified and independently validated as being critical for the transformation of contractile SMCs into an osteogenic phenotype promoting advanced, symptomatic atherosclerosis.
evidence.explanation: Supports smooth-muscle-cell transformation in advanced symptomatic atherosclerosis. It does not directly demonstrate plaque rupture or thrombosis, so it is retained here as partial support for the advanced plaque stage.

steps/8.description: Continued lipid accumulation, foam-cell death, and matrix remodeling produce a mature coronary atheroma with a necrotic lipid core beneath a fibrous cap. Expansion of the core and local plaque microenvironment can destabilize the cap and create a rupture-prone coronary lesion.

evidence.snippet: Destabilization is characterized by several different plaque phenotypes that cause major clinical events such as acute coronary syndrome and cerebrovascular strokes.
evidence.explanation: Histopathology and vascular-imaging evidence directly connects unstable atheroma phenotypes with acute coronary syndrome, supporting this terminal coronary consequence.

evidence.snippet: Endothelial erosion without rupture has more recently been shown to be a common phenotype to promote thrombosis as well.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports endothelial erosion as a thrombosis-promoting alternative to fibrous-cap rupture in the coronary consequence node.

steps/9.description: Rupture of an unstable coronary atheroma, or endothelial erosion over it, exposes thrombogenic material and triggers platelet activation, coagulation, and thrombotic coronary occlusion, causing acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction.

evidence.snippet: may suddenly cause life-threatening coronary thrombosis presenting as an acute coronary syndrome
evidence.explanation: Directly links rupture of a coronary atherosclerotic plaque to acute coronary syndrome, the mechanism by which myocardial infarction arises as a complication of coronary artery disease.

evidence.snippet: Arterial injury causes endothelial dysfunction promoting modification of apoB containing lipoproteins and infiltration of monocytes into the subendothelial space.
evidence.explanation: Links arterial injury and endothelial dysfunction to subendothelial apoB modification and monocyte entry, but does not isolate nitric-oxide loss or directly establish every intermediate in lipoprotein retention.

edges/0.description: Connects the vasomotor and disturbed-flow endothelial branch to the conserved retention trigger without asserting that reduced nitric oxide alone is sufficient for apoB retention.

evidence.snippet: Arterial injury causes endothelial dysfunction promoting modification of apoB containing lipoproteins and infiltration of monocytes into the subendothelial space.
evidence.explanation: Directly links endothelial injury and modified apoB lipoproteins to monocyte entry into the subendothelial space.

evidence.snippet: Macrophage inflammatory chemoattractants stimulate infiltration and proliferation of smooth muscle cells. Smooth muscle cells produce the extracellular matrix providing a stable fibrous barrier between plaque prothrombotic factors and platelets.
evidence.explanation: Connects macrophage inflammation to smooth-muscle-cell proliferation and extracellular-matrix production, the next core stage.

evidence.snippet: Unresolved inflammation results in formation of vulnerable plaques characterized by enhanced macrophage apoptosis and defective efferocytosis of apoptotic cells resulting in necrotic cell death leading to increased smooth muscle cell death, decreased extracellular matrix production, and collagen degradation by macrophage proteases.
evidence.explanation: Identifies macrophage/foam-cell death and extracellular-matrix remodeling as known intermediates in progression toward vulnerable advanced plaque.

edges/3.description: Continued lipid accumulation, foam-cell death, and matrix remodeling intervene between initial fibrofatty plaque assembly and advanced atheroma.

evidence.snippet: There are several rupture-associated phenotypes causing thrombotic vascular occlusion including simple fibrous cap rupture of an atheroma, fibrous cap rupture at site of previous rupture-and-repair of an atheroma, and nodular calcification with rupture.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports the causal transition from advanced atheroma rupture to thrombotic vascular occlusion.

edges/5.description: A mature, space-occupying coronary atheroma narrows the epicardial lumen so that coronary flow reserve is exhausted when myocardial oxygen demand rises, producing the exertional ischemia that is felt as angina pectoris.

edges/6.description: The same demand ischemia produced by a flow-limiting atheroma transiently impairs left ventricular relaxation and contraction, raising filling pressures and presenting as exertional breathlessness rather than as chest pain (an anginal equivalent).

evidence.snippet: may suddenly cause life-threatening coronary thrombosis presenting as an acute coronary syndrome
evidence.explanation: Directly links rupture of a coronary atherosclerotic plaque to acute coronary syndrome, the mechanism by which myocardial infarction arises as a complication of coronary artery disease.

edges/7.description: Thrombus forming on a ruptured or eroded coronary plaque occludes the epicardial vessel, and the resulting abrupt loss of downstream perfusion produces myocardial necrosis, i.e. the clinical infarct.

evidence.snippet: Smoking (odds ratio 2.87 for current vs never, PAR 35.7% for current and former vs never)
evidence.explanation: INTERHEART, a standardised case-control study of acute myocardial infarction across 52 countries with 15152 cases and 14820 controls. Establishes smoking as one of the largest modifiable contributors to population attributable risk.

edges/8.description: Tobacco smoking raises the risk of acute myocardial infarction in a dose-dependent way. The link is drawn to the clinical event because that is what the cited epidemiology measures; the mediating coronary mechanism is deliberately left unasserted here, as the entry's review notes require.

evidence.snippet: Higher compared to lower P:S ratio diets lowered LDL cholesterol (MD -15.72 mg/dL; 95% CI: -20.51, -10.92; I2 = 68%) when the test diets differed in SFA (≥2% kcal), but not when diets were SFA-matched (MD -3.45 mg/dL; 95% CI: -7.88, 0.98; I2 = 70%)
evidence.explanation: 24 randomised complete-feeding trials, n=1011. The design removes saturated fat rather than adding it, so the forward claim that saturated fat raises the atherogenic pool is inferred. The quote carries its own control: the LDL difference appears only where the diets differ in saturated fat and vanishes when they are saturated-fat-matched, which is what attributes the effect to saturated fat rather than to the fat substitution generally.

edges/9.description: Dietary saturated fat raises serum cholesterol, increasing the atherogenic lipoprotein pool available for retention in the coronary subendothelial space. The edge is recorded as predisposing through a serum-cholesterol intermediate rather than as a direct action on the retention step.

evidence.snippet: regular physical activity (0.86, PAR 12.2%)
evidence.explanation: INTERHEART reports regular physical activity as protective against myocardial infarction with a population attributable risk of 12.2 percent for its absence, which is the evidence that inactivity is a risk factor for this disease.

edges/10.description: Absence of regular physical activity is an independent contributor to myocardial infarction risk. The metabolic-syndrome route is not settled for sedentary behaviour specifically, so the intermediates are left unknown and the edge attaches to the clinical event the epidemiology measures.

evidence.snippet: abdominal obesity (1.12 for top vs lowest tertile and 1.62 for middle vs lowest tertile, PAR 20.1% for top two tertiles vs lowest tertile)
evidence.explanation: INTERHEART. Note the measure is abdominal obesity by waist/hip ratio rather than body mass index, which is a more specific claim than the entry name suggests.

edges/11.description: Abdominal obesity, measured by waist/hip ratio, is an independent contributor to myocardial infarction risk. The cited source establishes the association with the clinical event rather than a specific coronary mechanism, so the intermediates are recorded as unknown.

evidence.snippet: Compared with epsilon3/epsilon3, the odds ratio for coronary disease was 0.80 (95% CI, 0.70-0.90) in epsilon2 carriers and was 1.06 (95% CI, 0.99-1.13) in epsilon4 carriers.
evidence.explanation: Meta-analysis of 121 studies (37,850 coronary cases) quantifies the APOE genotype-coronary risk association, with epsilon2 carriers at lower risk than the epsilon3/epsilon3 reference.

evidence.snippet: Rare genetic mutations that cause reduced LDL receptor function lead to markedly higher LDL-C and a dose-dependent increase in the risk of ASCVD
evidence.explanation: EAS consensus statement establishes that loss of LDL-receptor function raises LDL-C and increases atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk in a dose-dependent manner.

evidence.snippet: these mutations were associated with a 28 percent reduction in mean LDL cholesterol and an 88 percent reduction in the risk of CHD
evidence.explanation: ARIC cohort shows PCSK9 nonsense variants lower LDL cholesterol and substantially reduce coronary heart disease incidence, establishing PCSK9 as a causal modifier of coronary risk.

evidence.snippet: Homozygotes for the risk allele make up 20 to 25% of Caucasians and have a approximately 30 to 40% increased risk of CHD.
evidence.explanation: Genome-wide association scanning identified the chromosome 9p21 interval as a common CHD risk locus, quantifying the effect size in risk-allele homozygotes.

evidence.snippet: The guidelines recommend that all patients with chronic coronary artery disease receive high-intensity lipid-lowering treatment, with a target LDL level of less than 1.4 mmol/L.
evidence.explanation: The ESC chronic-coronary-syndrome guidelines recommend high-intensity lipid-lowering therapy (statins) for all patients, targeting LDL below 1.4 mmol/L.

treatments/0.description: Lower LDL cholesterol and stabilize atherosclerotic plaques.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: By upregulating hepatic LDL-receptor activity and lowering circulating apoB-lipoprotein concentration, statins reduce the pool of lipoprotein available for retention in the coronary subendothelial space, damping the initiating step of atherogenesis.

treatments/0/targets/1.description: Statin therapy alters the composition of the mature atheroma toward a thicker fibrous cap and smaller lipid core, which is the plaque-stabilizing action referred to in this treatment's description.

evidence.snippet: A primary end-point event occurred in 17.2% of the patients in the icosapent ethyl group, as compared with 22.0% of the patients in the placebo group
evidence.explanation: REDUCE-IT directly establishes the randomized composite-event contrast in its selected high-risk, statin-treated population.

evidence.snippet: Among patients treated with icosapent ethyl versus placebo, there was a 34% reduction in the primary composite end point
evidence.explanation: This post hoc analysis of 3408 REDUCE-IT participants with prior PCI reported HR 0.66 (95% CI, 0.58-0.76) for this endpoint, supporting applicability of the randomized event contrast to a coronary subgroup. It does not identify a mediator, was not a separate randomized trial of coronary disease, and retains the parent trial's mineral-oil comparison.

evidence.snippet: A larger percentage of patients in the icosapent ethyl group than in the placebo group were hospitalized for atrial fibrillation or flutter (3.1% vs. 2.1%, P=0.004).
evidence.explanation: The randomized safety result bounds an unqualified cardioprotective interpretation.

evidence.snippet: Adverse events did not differ between the groups, but the rate of new-onset atrial fibrillation was significantly higher in the EPA group (3.1% versus 1.6%; P=0.017).
evidence.explanation: This randomized, open-label Japanese stable-CAD comparison of EPA 1.8 g/day with control independently supports an atrial-fibrillation safety signal without a mineral-oil placebo. Its different dose and design limit quantitative transfer to REDUCE-IT.

treatments/1.description: In REDUCE-IT, adjunctive icosapent ethyl 4 g/day reduced composite ischemic events versus a mineral-oil comparator in selected statin-treated adults with established cardiovascular disease or diabetes plus risk factors and persistent triglyceride elevation. Hospitalization for atrial fibrillation or flutter was more frequent. The trial population was broader than coronary artery disease alone, and neither the mediating mechanism nor the benefit magnitude versus an inert non-mineral-oil comparator is established.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Icosapent ethyl is placed at the mature-atheroma node because the candidate explanations for its randomized event reduction (plaque remodeling and atherogenic-particle lowering) both act there. The link is a hypothesis placement, not an established mediator: the entry's own description records that no mediating mechanism has been established.

evidence.snippet: allocation to antiplatelet therapy reduced the combined outcome of any serious vascular event by about one quarter; non-fatal myocardial infarction was reduced by one third, non-fatal stroke by one quarter, and vascular mortality by one sixth
evidence.explanation: Collaborative meta-analysis of randomised trials quantifies the reduction in serious vascular events, myocardial infarction, and vascular mortality achieved by antiplatelet therapy in high-risk patients.

treatments/2.description: Aspirin and P2Y12 inhibitors reduce thrombotic risk.

evidence.snippet: allocation to antiplatelet therapy reduced the combined outcome of any serious vascular event by about one quarter; non-fatal myocardial infarction was reduced by one third, non-fatal stroke by one quarter, and vascular mortality by one sixth
evidence.explanation: Collaborative meta-analysis of randomised trials quantifies the reduction in serious vascular events, myocardial infarction, and vascular mortality achieved by antiplatelet therapy in high-risk patients.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Aspirin and P2Y12 inhibitors blunt platelet activation and aggregation on exposed plaque contents, so a rupture or erosion is less likely to progress to an occlusive coronary thrombus.

treatments/3.description: Provide cardiovascular protection beyond blood pressure lowering.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibition lowers angiotensin II signalling and arterial wall stress at the endothelial-dysfunction node, which is the proposed locus of the cardiovascular protection this entry describes as going beyond blood-pressure lowering. The size of the non-haemodynamic component is not settled and no mediator is asserted here.

treatments/4.description: Reduce myocardial oxygen demand and prevent angina.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: Beta blockade lowers heart rate and contractility and so reduces myocardial oxygen demand, raising the exertional threshold at which a fixed coronary stenosis produces ischemic pain. This is a symptomatic action on the anginal manifestation rather than on the plaque itself.

treatments/5.description: Angioplasty with stenting to restore coronary blood flow.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Balloon angioplasty and stent implantation mechanically enlarge the lumen at the flow-limiting mature atheroma, restoring epicardial coronary flow without altering the lesion biology that produced it.

treatments/5/targets/1.description: In the acute setting, primary PCI reopens the thrombotically occluded vessel, restoring perfusion to myocardium distal to the ruptured plaque.

treatments/6.description: Surgical revascularization for severe multivessel disease.

treatments/6/targets/0.description: A graft carries blood to the myocardium distal to the diseased segment, routing around the flow-limiting atheroma rather than modifying it, which is why severe multivessel disease is treated this way.

evidence.snippet: The predominant mechanism for PGS×C is the amplification of genetic effects in adverse contexts, such as low polyunsaturated fatty acids or social determinants of ill health
evidence.explanation: Direct source (Nagpal & Gibson 2026): across seven UK Biobank diseases and 75 contexts, amplification of genetic effects in adverse contexts is identified as the predominant mechanism of PGS×context interaction — the mechanism applied in this hypothesis.

evidence.snippet: GxSex is pervasive but acts primarily through systematic sex differences in the magnitude of many genetic effects
evidence.explanation: Establishes amplification — systematic differences in the magnitude of polygenic effects rather than in the identity of causal variants — as the primary mode of gene-by-context interaction. Sex is among the contexts showing the strongest PGS×context amplification for CAD, so this supports amplification as the mechanism underlying the CAD PGS×C interactions modelled here.

hypotheses/0.description: Polygenic-score-by-context (PGS×C) interactions reported for coronary artery disease in the UK Biobank appear to be driven not by different causal variants acting in different environments, but by amplification: the same susceptibility loci (e.g. the 9p21 locus, APOE, LDLR, PCSK9) exert systematically larger effects in disease-promoting contexts. This entry proposes that the amplification arises because the polygenic liability and adverse exposures such as tobacco smoking converge on a shared upstream pathophysiology node — Endothelial Dysfunction — so their joint effect is super-additive on the liability-threshold scale rather than additive. Nagpal & Gibson (Nat Genet 2026, PMID:42443528) report that in past smokers with low omega-6 fatty acid levels the majority of CAD genetic effects are nearly perfectly correlated with, but up to twofold larger in magnitude than, those in non-smokers with higher omega-6 fatty acids, alongside an ~8% higher SNP-heritability — the signature of amplification rather than uncorrelated context-specific effects.

evidence.snippet: A total of 80 patients were enrolled in this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
evidence.explanation: EVAPORATE enrolled only 80. The cached abstract does not report how many participants contributed interpretable paired scans, so the effective analysis size and missing-scan sensitivity are not established by this exact evidence.

evidence.snippet: There was a significant reduction in the primary endpoint as IPE reduced LAP plaque volume by 17%, while in the placebo group LAP plaque volume more than doubled (+109%) (P = 0.0061).
evidence.explanation: The reported randomized contrast supports differential change in a CT-defined coronary plaque surrogate, not mediation of cardiovascular events or a specific cellular mechanism.

evidence.snippet: When further adjusted for age, sex, diabetes status, hypertension, and baseline TG, plaque volume changes between groups remained significantly different, P < 0.01.
evidence.explanation: Persistence after adjustment for baseline triglyceride is compatible with more than baseline-risk imbalance, but it is not a randomized mediation analysis of triglyceride response. The quoted adjustment list does not include baseline plaque, and the cached abstract does not report baseline plaque balance, so regression-to-the-mean sensitivity remains unresolved.

evidence.snippet: The PTV/EPA group showed a greater reduction in total atheroma volume compared to PTV group. IB-IVUS analyses revealed that lipid volume was significantly decreased during follow-up period in only PTV/EPA group.
evidence.explanation: CHERRY supplies an independent randomized coronary-imaging signal without the EVAPORATE mineral-oil comparison, but its open-label protocol tested EPA 1.8 g/day plus pitavastatin in 193 Japanese post-PCI patients for only 6–8 months, not IPE 4 g/day or event mediation.

evidence.snippet: There were no significant differences in the percent change for minimum FCT between the EPA or EPA+DHA group and the control group.
evidence.explanation: This 130-patient, three-arm trial limits the cap-stabilization version of the model because neither EPA 1.8 g/day nor mixed EPA/DHA produced a significantly greater overall minimum-FCT increase than statin-only control. The abstract reports a favorable minimum-FCT change in the subgroup below the median baseline FCT, but that subgroup does not overturn the null overall comparison. The trial does not refute the narrower plaque-volume signal or test IPE 4 g/day.

hypotheses/1.description: In statin-treated people with coronary atherosclerosis and persistent hypertriglyceridemia, icosapent ethyl may contribute to the observed cardiovascular-event contrast by altering coronary plaque composition or progression rather than through isolated change in circulating triglyceride concentration. EVAPORATE reported a randomized between-arm imaging signal, but its cached abstract reports 80 enrolled without the paired-scan analytic denominator or baseline plaque balance, and the reported multivariable model did not adjust for baseline plaque. Missing-scan and regression-to-the-mean sensitivity therefore remain unresolved. The trial also used a mineral-oil comparator and a surrogate endpoint and did not test whether plaque change mediated clinical events.

evidence.snippet: Compared with placebo (n = 211), IPE 4 g/day (n = 216) significantly reduced concentrations of: total (12.2%, P = .0002), large (46.4%, P < .0001), and medium (12.1%, P = .0068) very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) particles; total (7.7%, P = .0017) and small (13.5%, P < .0001) LDL particles
evidence.explanation: This prespecified exploratory 12-week NMR analysis supports an IPE-versus-placebo contrast in atherogenic particle concentrations, but it did not test coronary plaque, clinical events, or mediation. Without an inert third arm, it does not separate direct IPE action from comparator behavior.

evidence.snippet: Without increasing LDL-C, icosapent ethyl significantly reduced median TG (-20%; p < 0.0001), non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (-12.3%; p < 0.0001), total cholesterol (-11.1%; p < 0.0001), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (-5.2%; p = 0.0042), very LDL-C (-21.0%; p < 0.0001), very low-density lipoprotein TG (-22.9%; p < 0.0001), remnant lipoprotein cholesterol (-23.0%; p = 0.0125), apolipoprotein B (-7.4%; p = 0.0021)
evidence.explanation: This supplies the apolipoprotein-B and remnant-cholesterol arm of the particle-lowering model, which the nuclear-magnetic-resonance particle analysis above does not measure directly: randomized 12-week reductions in remnant lipoprotein cholesterol and apolipoprotein B occurred without an increase in LDL cholesterol. It remains a short-term biomarker contrast against the same oil-based comparator, measured no coronary plaque and no clinical events, and therefore leaves both the particle-to-plaque and the particle-to-event steps untested.

evidence.snippet: This post hoc analysis assessed 246 ANCHOR patients with baseline hsCRP ≥ 2.0 mg/L randomized to icosapent ethyl 4 g/day (n = 126; approved dose) or placebo (n = 120).
evidence.explanation: The apolipoprotein-B and remnant reductions quoted above come from 246 of the 702 randomized ANCHOR participants, selected after the fact for baseline high-sensitivity C-reactive protein at or above 2.0 mg/L. The randomization is preserved within that subset, but the analysis was not prespecified for these endpoints and does not establish the same effect sizes in the full trial population.

hypotheses/2.description: In statin-treated people with persistent triglyceride elevation, icosapent ethyl may contribute to plaque or event effects by lowering concentrations of atherogenic VLDL and LDL particles, thereby reducing arterial exposure or retention of apoB-containing particles. Short-duration ANCHOR analyses establish pharmacodynamic change but did not measure coronary plaque, clinical events, or treatment-to-particle-to-event mediation.

open_questions/0.rationale: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

evidence.snippet: 1,600 adults with CAD admitted between 2022 and 2024; 36 in-hospital deaths occurred
evidence.explanation: Retrospective clinical cohort reports the sample size and mortality event count that bound how much this exploratory score can be expected to establish.

evidence.snippet: Twenty demographic, clinical, laboratory, and instrumental variables were evaluated. The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality during the index hospitalization.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the outcome the score predicts and the size of the candidate variable pool it was selected from, which is what makes the six retained variables data-driven rather than pre-specified.

evidence.snippet: The exploratory six-variable score included age ≥57 years, estimated glomerular filtration rate <45 mL/min/1.73 m², body mass index ≥25 kg/m², troponin I ≥100, prior myocardial infarction, and current smoking.
evidence.explanation: Names the six variables the rationale lists. The snippet reproduces the cached preprint verbatim, including its HTML-escaped less-than sign.

evidence.snippet: showed modest discrimination for all-cause in-hospital mortality and should be regarded as a preliminary, hypothesis-generating risk-stratification approach
evidence.explanation: The authors' own caution that the score is preliminary, which is why this is curated as an open knowledge gap rather than as an asserted risk stratifier.

open_questions/1.rationale: An exploratory mortality risk score derived from 1,600 CAD-DAPT patients identified six variables associated with all-cause in-hospital mortality: age ≥57 years, estimated glomerular filtration rate <45 mL/min/1.73 m², body mass index ≥25 kg/m², elevated troponin I (≥100), prior myocardial infarction, and current smoking. However, the score showed only modest discrimination (AUC 0.61-0.654 across derivation and hold-out subsets) with only 36 outcome events; it is explicitly preliminary and not recommended for routine clinical use without external validation. Replication and mechanistic understanding of kidney dysfunction and troponin elevation as mortality predictors in the DAPT context remains a gap.

evidence.snippet: Icosapent ethyl has demonstrated reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events, although the mechanism of benefit remains incompletely understood and is not explained entirely by triglyceride lowering.
evidence.explanation: The seed review directly defines the unresolved mechanism but does not establish any proposed mediator.

evidence.snippet: Among participants in REDUCE-IT, allocation to icosapent ethyl had minimal effects on a series of biomarkers associated with atherosclerotic disease, whereas levels increased among those allocated to mineral oil.
evidence.explanation: Randomized longitudinal biomarker data show that relative inflammatory differences cannot be interpreted as direct biomarker lowering by icosapent ethyl.

evidence.snippet: The effect of these findings on interpretation of the overall risk reductions in clinical events observed within REDUCE-IT is uncertain.
evidence.explanation: The investigators explicitly preserve uncertainty about how mineral-oil biomarker changes affect interpretation of the event contrast.

evidence.snippet: Icosapent ethyl treatment resulted in a numerically lower risk of cardiovascular events that did not reach statistical significance in patients with chronic coronary artery disease, a low EPA/AA ratio, and statin treatment.
evidence.explanation: This 1.8-g/day, open-label Japanese stable-CAD trial reported a nonsignificant primary endpoint. Its direction is compatible with a product effect outside the REDUCE-IT comparison, but it neither establishes a mechanism nor quantifies any mineral-oil contribution.

evidence.snippet: Meanwhile, the secondary composite end point of coronary events in the EPA group was significantly lower
evidence.explanation: The reported HR was 0.73 (95% CI, 0.55-0.97). This significant secondary coronary composite supplies event evidence from a comparison that did not use mineral oil in chronic CAD, but it was a secondary endpoint in an open-label Japanese trial of EPA 1.8 g/day and did not test mediation.

evidence.snippet: Participants were randomized to receive 4 g/d of omega-3 CA (n = 6539) or corn oil, which was intended to serve as an inert comparator (n = 6539), in addition to usual background therapies, including statins.
evidence.explanation: STRENGTH supplies a comparison that did not use mineral oil, although corn oil was intended rather than independently proven to be inert.

evidence.snippet: Among statin-treated patients at high cardiovascular risk, the addition of omega-3 CA, compared with corn oil, to usual background therapies resulted in no significant difference in a composite outcome of major adverse cardiovascular events.
evidence.explanation: The neutral event result constrains a formulation-agnostic omega-3 cardioprotection claim. STRENGTH tested an EPA/DHA carboxylic-acid formulation rather than purified IPE, so it does not refute an IPE-specific mechanism.

open_questions/2.rationale: REDUCE-IT established an ischemic-event contrast between icosapent ethyl and a mineral-oil comparator but did not identify a mediator. The seed review explicitly states that triglyceride lowering does not fully explain the benefit. The small 80-patient EVAPORATE trial observed differential CT-plaque change against mineral oil after adjustment for baseline triglyceride, but plaque is a surrogate and the study did not test treatment-to-plaque-to-event mediation. In the REDUCE-IT biomarker substudy, icosapent ethyl produced minimal change in several inflammatory and lipid-oxidation markers while those markers increased among participants assigned to mineral oil; without an inert third arm, relative biomarker differences do not establish direct icosapent lowering or mineral-oil causation. Focused research found a lower-dose EPA plaque-volume signal in CHERRY, no overall fibrous-cap-thickness benefit in a separate three-arm trial, and short-term IPE-associated atherogenic-particle reductions in ANCHOR; none tested clinical mediation. A post hoc REDUCE-IT prior-PCI subgroup supports transfer of the event contrast to coronary disease but remains a subgroup analysis against mineral oil. RESPECT-EPA, an open-label 1.8-g/day Japanese stable-CAD trial without an oil placebo, reported a nonsignificant primary endpoint, a significant secondary coronary composite, and more new-onset atrial fibrillation; it supplies a coronary signal from a comparison that did not use mineral oil but does not establish a mechanism. STRENGTH found no event benefit for a distinct EPA/DHA carboxylic-acid formulation against corn oil intended as an inert comparator. That result constrains class-wide omega-3 inference but does not directly test purified IPE or distinguish its candidate pathways. Plaque remodeling; remnant-particle composition, number, trafficking, and arterial retention; platelet biology; specialized inflammatory resolution; endothelial function; and membrane or lipid-oxidation effects remain candidates rather than established mechanisms. Baseline-subgroup, achieved-EPA, and other postrandomization associations cannot substitute for randomized temporal mediation.

evidence.snippet: The W290G mutation was found in exon IIIa which is common to both alternatively spliced forms of FGFR2, BEK (expressed predominantly in primordial bones) and KGFR (expressed preferentially in epithelia). steps/4.description: ERK1/2-driven FGFR2 signaling accelerates osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization within cranial suture mesenchyme, producing excess osteogenic activity across the suture.

genes/0.notes: Over 40 different FGFR2 mutations have been identified. Common mutations include C342Y, C342R, and C342S in the Ig-III domain. Unlike Apert syndrome, Crouzon alleles are distributed across multiple exons (7, 8, 9, 10) rather than concentrated in a single hotspot. Exon IIIa alleles such as W290G affect sequence shared by the IIIb and IIIc isoforms and may broaden epithelial involvement. Several alleles overlap with Jackson-Weiss and Pfeiffer syndromes, indicating that mutation position, splice-form context, and background modifiers all contribute to whether an FGFR2 craniosynostosis presents as Crouzon syndrome.

steps/1.description: Homozygous nonsense or frameshift variants in LTBP1. In the four reported families the alterations fall in the second EGF-like domain (c.1342C>T), the third EGF-like domain (c.4844del), and the 12th and 13th calcium-binding EGF-like domains (c.3991dup and c.4431T>A) of the long isoform. The position matters mechanistically and the two branches below are not interchangeable.

evidence.snippet: immunofluorescent analysis at 9 days post confluency (dpc) shows complete absence of LTBP1 in dermal fibroblasts of F4:II-1
evidence.explanation: Protein-level confirmation that the transcript loss produces an absent protein rather than a reduced one.

steps/2.description: The c.1342C>T transcript is degraded, and no LTBP1 protein reaches the matrix. This is the branch in which the expected TGF-beta abnormality does not appear.

evidence.snippet: Total TGFβ protein levels are significantly increased in conditioned media of F1:IV-2, but not of F4:II-1, compared to control subjects

evidence.snippet: This may suggest either notable redundancy between LTBP isoforms or that there are significant LTBP-independent mechanisms of TGFβ secretion and signaling that occur during development.

steps/3.description: Why complete absence of LTBP1 produces no TGF-beta signature. In the c.1342C>T fibroblasts total TGF-beta, the pSmad2/Smad2 ratio, POSTN expression and collagen I and III fiber incorporation are all unchanged, and LTBP2, LTBP3 and LTBP4 are available to carry the latent complex. Proposed by the authors rather than demonstrated - no paralog knockdown was performed in these cells.

evidence.snippet: In this study, we show that LTBP1 coordinates the incorporation of fibrillin-1 and -2 into the extracellular matrix in vitro.

evidence.snippet: Thereby our findings uncover a novel TGFβ-independent LTBP1 function potentially contributing to the development of connective tissue disorders.

evidence.snippet: also show a significant reduction of binding affinity of the N-terminal regions of fibrillin-1 (8- to 12-fold) and fibrillin-2 (16- to 40-fold) to either mutant LTBP1 fragment

steps/5.description: The c.4844del transcript escapes decay and a truncated protein is made. Recombinant C-terminal fragments carrying c.4844del or c.4431T>A bind the N-terminal regions of fibrillin-1 and fibrillin-2 far more weakly than control fragment, by surface plasmon resonance and by solid-phase binding in both directions.

evidence.snippet: Reduced LTBP1 binding to fibrillin-containing microfibrils would yield in large latency complexes (LLCs) that fail to be targeted correctly to the ECM, resulting in their inappropriate activation.

steps/6.description: Truncated LTBP1 still forms fibers, but only rudimentary ones, and the large latent complex it carries is no longer held securely in the microfibril network. The authors' proposal is that latent complexes which fail to be targeted to the matrix are activated inappropriately.

genes/0.notes:
All four reported alleles are premature termination codons, and it would be natural to record the gene as simply loss of function. The functional work argues against collapsing them that way. The one N-terminal allele tested undergoes nonsense-mediated decay and behaves as a null; the C-terminal alleles escape decay and produce a protein that is made, secreted, and incorporated into rudimentary fibers while binding fibrillin poorly - a protein present and misbehaving rather than absent. The functional_impact_category on the initiating pathophysiology node is recorded as LOSS_OF_FUNCTION because that is what the authors demonstrate for the alleles at the protein-function level, but the downstream cellular phenotype of the C-terminal class is one of excess matrix and excess signaling.
Two fibroblast lines is the entire functional dataset, one allele per class, so the split is a two-sample observation and the authors say so explicitly. No genotype-phenotype correlation can be drawn from the clinical data either: the individual without craniosynostosis and the individual with severe intellectual disability carry different alleles from each other, and the numbers are far too small to test.

hypotheses/0.description:
The TGF-beta abnormality demonstrated in ARCL2E is an increase, and it was measured in dermal fibroblasts from one individual carrying a C-terminal allele. The authors argue that the skeletal phenotype may require the opposite: craniosynostosis has been produced in mice by reducing TGF-beta bioavailability in the bone matrix through Ltbp3 ablation, and skull deformities are reported in Ltbp1-null mice. Under this model the direction of the TGF-beta change is set by the local matrix rather than by the variant, so dermis and cranial suture can move in opposite directions from the same genotype.
Nothing in the published work measures TGF-beta in human ARCL2E bone or suture tissue, so the skeletal limb of this model is unmeasured. A competing possibility the same authors raise is that the relevant LTBP1 function in bone is not TGF-beta handling at all.

evidence.snippet: Further studies are needed to confirm the distinct molecular consequences related to a loss of LTBP1 or altered LTBP1 level in cultured dermal fibroblast samples derived from other diagnosed individuals with LTBP1 variants in similar regions.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, we identified potentially relevant variants in 87% of the remaining families with no previously detected causal variants, including novel variants in ADAMTSL4, ASH1L, ATRX, C2CD3, CHD5, ERF, H4C5, IFT122, IFT140, KDM6B, KMT2D, LTBP1, MAP3K7, NOTCH2, NSD1, SOS1, SPRY1, POLR2A, PRRX1, RECQL4, TAB2, TAOK1, TET3, TGFBR1, TCF20, and ZBTB20.
evidence.explanation: Graded NO_EVIDENCE because this names LTBP1 in a list of potentially relevant candidate variants in a craniosynostosis cohort without zygosity, segregation or functional data. It does not bear on whether biallelic LTBP1 truncation causes this disorder, and is recorded here so it is not mistaken for a second cohort.

open_questions/0.rationale:
The disorder rests on one publication. Every frequency in this entry is a fraction of eight, every functional claim about the branch split comes from two fibroblast lines, and the ascertainment was entirely through consanguineous families identified by research sequencing. What a non-consanguineous compound heterozygote looks like is unknown, and so is whether the N-terminal and C-terminal classes differ clinically rather than only in cell culture.
The only other human LTBP1 finding located is a candidate variant in a craniosynostosis sequencing cohort, reported without segregation, zygosity or functional work, and grouped by its authors with other variants of uncertain relevance. It is a lead for where the second cohort might come from, not a replication.

evidence.snippet: Remarkably, Ltbp1L−/− and Ltbp1−/− mice present with truncus arteriosus, interrupted aortic arch, and perinatal lethality. Our observations imply differences in functional redundancy of LTBP family members or other compensatory mechanisms for Ltbp1 deficiency in mice versus humans and teleosts.
evidence.explanation: States the mismatch and the authors' proposed explanation for it.

evidence.snippet: Assessment of cardiovascular function in adult zebrafish by ultrasound imaging, however, revealed no significant differences between ltbp1−/−Δ29 zebrafish, ltbp1−/−Δ35 zebrafish, and corresponding WT siblings at 10 months of age
evidence.explanation: The zebrafish result, which sides with the human phenotype rather than the mouse one.

open_questions/1.rationale:
Ltbp1L-null and Ltbp1-null mice die perinatally with persistent truncus arteriosus and interrupted aortic arch, from decreased TGF-beta activity in the outflow tract. Humans homozygous for premature truncating LTBP1 variants have no conotruncal defect, survive into adolescence at least, and show mild variable cardiac findings instead. The zebrafish lines have normal cardiac function on ultrasound. The mismatch is not a detail: it is the reason the mouse literature cannot be used to counsel cardiac risk in this disorder, and it is a specific argument that LTBP paralog redundancy differs between species.
It also cuts the other way. The absence of a severe cardiac phenotype in eight humans is not the same as its absence in the disorder, and the oldest individual reported was 17 years 5 months. Adult cardiovascular outcome in ARCL2E is simply unobserved.

evidence.snippet: However, neither craniofacial abnormalities nor craniosynostosis were observed in both homozygous mutant zebrafish models.
evidence.explanation: The negative result at the heart of this mismatch.

evidence.snippet: A possible explanation for the lack of these features could be the induction of genetic compensation mechanisms, which could partly rescue the craniosynostosis phenotype.
evidence.explanation: The authors' proposed explanation, offered as a possibility.

open_questions/2.rationale:
Craniosynostosis is present in three-quarters of affected humans and is the feature that separates this disorder from the rest of the cutis laxa group, yet neither zebrafish line develops it - the interfrontal, coronal, sagittal and lambdoid sutures are all normal, as is craniofacial morphology. The mouse literature offers only minor craniofacial abnormalities in an Ltbp1-null. So the single most diagnostically useful feature of ARCL2E currently has no animal model, and the proposed reduced-TGF-beta-in-bone mechanism has never been tested in a system that produces the phenotype.
The authors suggest genetic compensation, or residual mutant transcript, as reasons the fish may be protected, and propose an RNA-less allele as the test. Neither explanation has been evaluated.
