evidence.snippet: These findings could explain the dominant negative effect of heterozygous mutation on SLFN14 expression in patients' platelets.
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL because the source frames the dominant-negative reading as an explanation its data could support rather than one it demonstrates.

steps/2.description:
SLFN14 protein is markedly reduced in patient platelets and in cells transfected with the mutant construct. The reduction is post-translational: the variants partially misfold and are degraded, and because the mutant protein also oligomerises, the wild-type product made from the normal allele is dragged down with it. That is the proposed basis of dominance.
Curated as ESTABLISHED because the measurement itself - less protein in patient platelets - is reproduced across reports. What is contested is whether losing protein is the whole story, which is the point of the competing node below.

evidence.snippet: IT-linked mutations alter SLFN14 RNA substrate specificity, enhancing depletion of type II tRNAs while reducing rRNA cleavage.
evidence.explanation: The substrate shift itself, which is the whole of this node's claim.

evidence.snippet: Most IT-associated mutations in the RNase domain reduce RNA cleavage activity in vitro
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL and cited deliberately against this node: the same paper records the prior in-vitro consensus that these mutations reduce activity, which is what the dominant-negative account rests on.

steps/3.description:
The competing account. Rather than simply having less enzyme, patient variants have an enzyme that prefers different substrates: depletion of type II tRNAs is enhanced while cleavage of ribosomal RNA is reduced. That is a change in what the enzyme does, not only in how much of it there is.
The distinction matters because the two accounts point opposite ways therapeutically. If the lesion is loss of SLFN14, restoring or stabilising the protein is the goal. If the lesion is redirected activity, restoring the protein would deliver more of the wrong enzymatic activity, and inhibiting it would be closer to right.
PROVISIONAL: the work is in an overexpression cell system rather than in megakaryocytes or patient cells, and no experiment has yet distinguished the two accounts in the lineage that actually fails.

evidence.snippet: SLFN14-defective platelets and mature MK showed signs of rRNA degradation; however, this was absent in undifferentiated imMKCL cells and granulocytes.
evidence.explanation: Both halves matter: the rRNA abnormality, and its restriction to mature cells of this lineage, which is what makes it a plausible explanation for a lineage-specific disease.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that all SLFN14 variants colocalize with ribosomes and mediate rRNA endonucleolytic degradation.

evidence.snippet: This shift promotes ribosome stalling at codons decoded by type II tRNAs, triggering global translational arrest, stress signaling, and cell death.
evidence.explanation: The translational consequence proposed by the altered-specificity account, which is why this node names tRNA decay alongside rRNA turnover.

steps/4.description: Whichever route reaches it, the shared consequence is that RNA turnover on the ribosome is no longer normal in this lineage. Patient platelets and mature megakaryocytes show signs of ribosomal RNA degradation, and the observation is lineage- and stage-restricted - it is absent from undifferentiated megakaryocytic cells and from granulocytes, which is the clearest evidence that the defect only bites where SLFN14 normally works hardest.

hypotheses/0.description: The variants destabilise the protein, which is degraded post-translationally; because SLFN14 oligomerises, mutant subunits also reduce the wild-type pool, giving dominance from what is fundamentally a loss of enzyme. This is the older account and the one the measured reduction of SLFN14 in patient platelets most directly supports.

evidence.snippet: IT-linked mutations alter SLFN14 RNA substrate specificity, enhancing depletion of type II tRNAs while reducing rRNA cleavage.
evidence.explanation: The substrate shift that defines this hypothesis.

hypotheses/1.description: The variants do not merely reduce activity but change which RNAs are cleaved, driving type II tRNA depletion, ribosome stalling and translational arrest. On this account the disease is caused by an activity the mutant enzyme has, not by one it lacks - which inverts the therapeutic goal.

open_questions/0.rationale:
Both accounts are supported by real data and they are not compatible.
The loss account has the more direct clinical observation behind it: SLFN14 protein is markedly reduced in patient platelets, the reduction is explained by misfolding and post-translational degradation, and oligomerisation gives a route to dominance. Most disease-associated RNase-domain mutations reduce cleavage activity in vitro.
The redirection account explains something the loss account does not. If the lesion were simply less enzyme, a heterozygote with roughly half-normal activity should be mildly affected in proportion; instead these variants shift which RNAs are cleaved, deplete type II tRNAs, stall ribosomes and trigger cell death - an active injury rather than a shortfall.
The distinction is not academic. If the disease is loss of SLFN14, a therapy should restore or stabilise the protein. If it is redirected activity, restoring the protein delivers more of the harmful activity and inhibition is the rational goal. A therapeutic programme cannot be designed until this is settled.
Neither body of work has been done in megakaryocytes. The degradation studies used transfected cell lines; the substrate-specificity study used HEK293T overexpression. The lineage where the disease actually happens has not been used to test either.

open_questions/1.rationale:
This is a mismatch rather than a gap: the model exists, the result is clear, and it disagrees with the patients. Homozygous K208N mice have microcytic erythrocytosis and die in utero; heterozygotes have anaemia and splenomegaly. Neither shows the bleeding or platelet defect that defines the human disease.
SLFN14 is expressed in both megakaryocyte and erythroid precursors, so a shift in which of the two is rate-limiting between species is a plausible explanation - and it is only that. It has not been tested.
It matters for how the rest of the model evidence is read. The conditional knockout that does reproduce bleeding was made by deleting the gene in the megakaryocyte lineage, which guarantees a megakaryocyte phenotype by construction. It shows what losing SLFN14 in megakaryocytes does; it does not show that the patient variants do that.

evidence.snippet: Podoconiosis is a tropical lymphedema resulting from long-term barefoot exposure to red-clay soil derived from volcanic rock. The World Health Organization recently designated it as a neglected tropical disease. Podoconiosis develops in only a subgroup of exposed people, and studies have shown familial clustering with high heritability (63%).
evidence.explanation: The canonical statement of the exposure and its duration.

evidence.snippet: Nine studies found a correlation between podoconiosis occurrence and regions with underlying alkalic volcanic bedrock, and six linked pedogenic factors (altitude and rainfall) with disease occurrence. Several studies linked specific soil mineralogy and geochemistry with endemic regions, including an abundance of phyllosilicate clay minerals, quartz, and trace elements, notably iron, beryllium and zirconium.
evidence.explanation: The bedrock, pedogenic and mineralogical correlates that make this a geochemically defined exposure rather than a geographic one.

evidence.snippet: However, it remains unclear whether these are covariates or direct contributors to the pathogenesis of the disease
evidence.explanation: The systematic review's own caution that the mineral correlations may be covariates rather than causes. Curated because this entry names specific minerals and should not imply more than the source does.

evidence.snippet: Podoconiosis is a tropical lymphedema resulting from long-term barefoot exposure to red-clay soil derived from volcanic rock. The World Health Organization recently designated it as a neglected tropical disease. Podoconiosis develops in only a subgroup of exposed people, and studies have shown familial clustering with high heritability (63%).
evidence.explanation: States the exposure and its duration, which is what this node records, and the heritability figure that makes the exposure necessary rather than sufficient.

evidence.snippet: Nine studies found a correlation between podoconiosis occurrence and regions with underlying alkalic volcanic bedrock, and six linked pedogenic factors (altitude and rainfall) with disease occurrence. Several studies linked specific soil mineralogy and geochemistry with endemic regions, including an abundance of phyllosilicate clay minerals, quartz, and trace elements, notably iron, beryllium and zirconium.
evidence.explanation: The systematic review's bedrock and pedogenic correlations, and the mineral inventory that the next node's particles come from.

evidence.snippet: Walking barefoot adjusted odd ratio (AOR) 5.35 (95% CI: 1.65, 9.05), p = 0.001, not washing feet with soap and water regularly AOR 2.8 (95% CI: 1.16, 4.44, p = 0.001), and an increased age AOR 2.23 (95% CI: 1.25, 5.58) were factors significantly associated with the prevalence of podoconiosis.
evidence.explanation: The effect estimate for the behaviour itself - walking barefoot carries an adjusted odds ratio above five in pooled sub-Saharan data.

steps/2.description: The necessary exposure. Subsistence farmers working barefoot on red clay weathered from alkalic volcanic bedrock accumulate contact over years to decades. The soil is the operative agent, not the terrain: endemicity tracks bedrock geochemistry and the pedogenic conditions that produce these clays - high altitude and high rainfall - rather than any vector distribution.

evidence.snippet: The presence of microparticles of clay is demonstrated in the dermis of the foot in a patient with endemic elephantiasis. The particles are seen to be in the phagosomes of macrophages or in the cytoplasm of other cells.
evidence.explanation: The direct demonstration that clay microparticles are present in the dermal tissue of an affected foot.

evidence.snippet: The predominant silica particles were mainly of the kaolinite type, sized between 0.2 and 2 µm
evidence.explanation: Gives the dominant mineral species and its size range, which is what makes transdermal entry mechanically plausible. Graded OTHER because the sentence is this paper's summary of the earlier microanalysis literature, not its own measurement.

steps/3.description: Colloid-sized silicate particles cross the plantar and dorsal skin of the foot and lodge in the dermis. Their identity is partly known and partly not: kaolinite predominates in lymph node microanalysis at 0.2-2 micrometres, and endemic soils are enriched in smectite, mica, quartz, iron oxides, beryllium and zirconium - but which constituent is the operative trigger has never been established.

evidence.snippet: The presence of microparticles of clay is demonstrated in the dermis of the foot in a patient with endemic elephantiasis. The particles are seen to be in the phagosomes of macrophages or in the cytoplasm of other cells.
evidence.explanation: The particles inside macrophage phagosomes, which is precisely this node's claim.

evidence.snippet: The disease develops in only some people exposed to irritant soils, although mineral particles can be seen in the lymphatic system and lymph nodes of unaffected as well as affected people.
evidence.explanation: The observation that makes this node insufficient on its own: particles are present in unaffected people too. Curated here because it is the reason the HLA node exists.

steps/4.description: Dermal macrophages engulf the silicate particles. This step is not itself pathological - particles are found in the lymph nodes of unaffected residents of endemic areas too, which is why the entry treats deposition as necessary and the host response as what separates disease from exposure.

evidence.snippet: mineral particles in red-clay soils are absorbed through the skin of the foot and engulfed by macrophages in the lower limb lymphatic system, inducing an inflammatory response in the lymphatic vessels, which results in fibrosis and obstruction of the vessel lumen.
evidence.explanation: States the transport-to-lymphatics model this node represents, and names the inflammatory consequence the downstream nodes carry.

evidence.snippet: Silicate particles of the kaolinite and aluminum types have been identified in femoral lymph node biopsy samples from endemic area residents, suggesting a possible role in the pathogenesis of podoconiosis.
evidence.explanation: Locates the particles in femoral lymph node biopsies, the endpoint of the transport this node describes. Graded OTHER: background prose citing the earlier microanalysis literature, not this study's own result.

steps/5.description: Particle-laden macrophages migrate into the lower-limb lymphatic vessels and on to the regional lymph nodes, where the silicates are recoverable by microanalysis. From here the chain forks: one arm needs the HLA class II susceptibility, the other does not.

evidence.snippet: We found a genomewide significant association of podoconiosis with the single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs17612858, located 5.8 kb from the HLA-DQA1 locus (in the allelic model: odds ratio, 2.44; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.82 to 3.26; P=1.42×10(-9); and in the additive model: odds ratio, 2.19; 95% CI, 1.66 to 2.90; P=3.44×10(-8))
evidence.explanation: The genome-wide significant signal that anchors this node, with its effect size.

evidence.snippet: HLA typing showed the alleles HLA-DRB1*0701 (odds ratio, 2.00), DQA1*0201 (odds ratio, 1.91), and DQB1*0202 (odds ratio, 1.79) and the HLA-DRB1*0701-DQB1*0202 haplotype (odds ratio, 1.92) were risk variants for podoconiosis.
evidence.explanation: The classical HLA typing behind the SNP association, naming the risk alleles and the haplotype.

evidence.snippet: Association between variants in HLA class II loci with podoconiosis (a noncommunicable disease) suggests that the condition may be a T-cell-mediated inflammatory disease and is a model for gene-environment interactions that may be relevant to other complex genetic disorders.
evidence.explanation: Graded INDIRECT because the T-cell interpretation follows from the class II association by inference; the authors state it as a suggestion, and no antigen-specific T-cell response has been demonstrated.

evidence.snippet: Fourteen SNPs in the HLA class II region showed significant genome-wide association (P < 5.0 × 10-8) with podoconiosis. The lead SNP was rs9270911 (P = 5.51 × 10-10; OR 1.53; 95% CI 1.34-1.74), located near HLA-DRB1.
evidence.explanation: The replication in a larger, three-population sample, with its own lead SNP near HLA-DRB1.

evidence.snippet: Our findings confirm the HLA class II association with podoconiosis suggesting HLA-mediated abnormal induction and regulation of immune responses may have a direct role in its pathogenesis.
evidence.explanation: The replication study's own reading of what the association implies, again hedged - "may have a direct role" - which is the strength this node claims.

evidence.snippet: Gene ontology analysis showed differentially expressed genes to be closely related to major histocompatibility complex protein, cytokine and TNF receptor binding genes. Pathway enrichment analysis revealed involvement of lymphocyte activation, adaptive immunity, cytokine signalling, antigen processing and the IL-12 pathways.
evidence.explanation: The functional bridge from the genetic association to a mechanism: the differentially expressed genes in affected lymph node tissue enrich for MHC protein and antigen processing, which is what a class II association predicts and had not previously been shown.

evidence.snippet: NanoString technology was used to assess expression of 579 immune-related genes in formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded lymph node archival samples from podoconiosis patients and unaffected controls.
evidence.explanation: Records that the measurement was made in lymph node tissue rather than blood, which is what makes it evidence about the lesion site.

steps/6.description: The susceptibility step. Genome-wide association in Ethiopian populations places the signal squarely in the HLA class II region, replicated across three ethnic groups and with no other locus reaching significance in a better-powered second study. A class II association in a non-communicable disease is read as a CD4 T-cell-mediated response - but the antigen itself is unidentified, and whether the mineral is presented, modifies a self peptide, or binds the groove directly is unknown. Berylliosis is the explicit comparator.

evidence.snippet: Peripheral blood immunophenotyping of T cells indicated podoconiosis patients had significantly higher CD4 and CD8 T cell surface HLA-DR expression compared to healthy controls while CD62L expression was significantly lower.
evidence.explanation: The T-cell activation phenotype this node records, against endemic healthy controls.

evidence.snippet: The levels of the activation markers CD40 and CD86 were significantly higher on monocytes and dendritic cell subsets in patients compared to the controls.
evidence.explanation: The antigen-presenting-cell arm of the same activation state.

evidence.snippet: Our finding provides evidence that podoconiosis is associated with high levels of immune activation and inflammation with over-expression of genes within the pro-inflammatory axis.
evidence.explanation: The study's summary claim, which is what this node asserts.

evidence.snippet: Our results showed that the levels of TNF-α and IL-1β from in vitro cell cultures were significantly higher in unstimulated samples from patients compared to controls (p = 0.04 and p = 0.005, respectively).
evidence.explanation: The baseline cytokine difference, measured without stimulation, which is the "at rest" part of this node's claim.

evidence.snippet: The minerals kaolinite and chlorite induced two and three-fold higher levels of IL-1β following 24 h of stimulation in healthy controls compared to patients, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Counterintuitive and load-bearing. On stimulation with kaolinite and chlorite it was the healthy endemic controls, not the patients, who produced more IL-1beta - the opposite of what a hypersensitivity model predicts. It is graded SUPPORT because it supports *this* node's claim, a chronically activated or exhausted immune state, rather than the hypersensitivity reading; `supports` is relative to the record it sits on, and no node in this entry asserts hypersensitivity for it to refute. The argument is carried in the `podo_inverted_mineral_response` discussion.

steps/7.description: Patients carry a measurably activated immune system at rest: raised HLA-DR on circulating CD4 and CD8 T cells, raised CD40 and CD86 on monocytes and dendritic cells, lower CD62L, and higher unstimulated TNF-alpha and IL-1beta than endemic controls. The activation is systemic, not confined to the affected limb.

evidence.snippet: Intralymphatic silica provoked an immediate and intense macrophage reaction with later fibrosis both within lymph vessels and to a lesser extent within lymph nodes. Lymphography indicated that the consequent obstruction resulted more from the effects of silica on vessels than on nodes.
evidence.explanation: The macrophage reaction within lymph vessels, and the finding that the vessel is the dominant site over the node.

evidence.snippet: A moderate lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate was joined by mast cells and scattered macrophages; neutrophils and eosinophils were sparse.
evidence.explanation: The human counterpart, so this node does not rest on rabbit data alone: the infiltrate in affected human skin is lymphoplasmacytic with mast cells and macrophages, and conspicuously not neutrophilic.

evidence.snippet: Price also observed that silicate particles caused subendothelial edema, endolymphangitis, collagenisation and obliteration of the lymphatic lumen
evidence.explanation: Names subendothelial oedema and endolymphangitis in human tissue, which is this node's exact claim. Graded OTHER and INDIRECT because the sentence is this paper's summary of Price's earlier work rather than its own result.

steps/8.description: Inflammation of the lymphatic vessel wall, with subendothelial oedema and a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate. This is the lesion the two upstream arms - the HLA-restricted response and the direct particle effect - converge on.

evidence.snippet: Price also observed that silicate particles caused subendothelial edema, endolymphangitis, collagenisation and obliteration of the lymphatic lumen
evidence.explanation: Names collagenisation of the lymphatic wall in sequence with the obliteration it causes, which is the split this pair of nodes represents. Graded OTHER and INDIRECT: the sentence summarises Price's earlier work rather than reporting this paper's own result.

evidence.snippet: Dermal collagen bundles were thickened, and elastic fibers were dramatically reduced.
evidence.explanation: The collagen deposition, measured in affected human skin.

steps/9.description: Sustained inflammation lays down collagen in and around the lymphatic vessel wall. This is the fibrogenic process; the closed lumen it produces is the next node.

evidence.snippet: The conducting lymphatic in the subdermal tissue is found to be impermeable to Patent Blue Violet dye and to be fibrosed.
evidence.explanation: The functional demonstration that the fibrosed vessel no longer conducts - dye impermeability alongside the histological fibrosis.

evidence.snippet: Stage 3-5 disease was histopathologically characterised by epidermal and dermal thickening, verrucous acanthosis, inflammatory cell infiltrates (predominantly lymphoplasmacytic), dilated and ectatic and a reduced number of lymphatic vessels, eccrine ductal hyperplasia, and sclerosis such as thickened collagen bundles.
evidence.explanation: The advanced-stage histopathology, which reports a reduced number of lymphatic vessels alongside the sclerosis.

steps/10.description: The end state of the fibrosis: vessels that no longer carry lymph. Biopsy series count fewer lymphatic vessels in affected skin, and a subdermal conducting lymphatic in an affected foot was shown to be fibrosed and impermeable to injected dye - the functional proof, not just the histological one.

evidence.snippet: Stage 3-5 disease was histopathologically characterised by epidermal and dermal thickening, verrucous acanthosis, inflammatory cell infiltrates (predominantly lymphoplasmacytic), dilated and ectatic and a reduced number of lymphatic vessels, eccrine ductal hyperplasia, and sclerosis such as thickened collagen bundles.
evidence.explanation: The dermal half of the advanced-stage histopathology - thickening and sclerosis with thickened collagen bundles.

evidence.snippet: Dermal collagen bundles were thickened, and elastic fibers were dramatically reduced.
evidence.explanation: The second biopsy series' account of the same change, adding the elastic fibre loss.

steps/11.description: Chronic stasis lays down collagen in the dermis, producing thickened sclerotic bundles and the firm nodules of established disease. Nodules are present in about two fifths of patients and are what nodulectomy removes.

evidence.snippet: 220 (77.5%) patients had warty lesions, 114 (39.4%) had nodules.
evidence.explanation: The frequencies of warty lesions and nodules in a 289-patient series.

evidence.snippet: Stage 3-5 disease was histopathologically characterised by epidermal and dermal thickening, verrucous acanthosis, inflammatory cell infiltrates (predominantly lymphoplasmacytic), dilated and ectatic and a reduced number of lymphatic vessels, eccrine ductal hyperplasia, and sclerosis such as thickened collagen bundles.
evidence.explanation: The epidermal half of the same histopathology - epidermal thickening and verrucous acanthosis.

evidence.snippet: These include dermal nodules and a rough, velvet-like appearance to the skin known as mossy changes which are pathognomonic for the disease.
evidence.explanation: States that the mossy change is pathognomonic, which is why this node carries diagnostic weight rather than only descriptive weight.

steps/12.description: The epidermis thickens into verrucous acanthosis and the warty "mossy" plaques the disease is named for, present in about three quarters of patients. Curated separately from the dermal change because it is a different tissue layer and, more importantly, a different claim: this is where the skin stops being a barrier, and it is the node that leads to the acute attacks.

evidence.snippet: mineral particles in red-clay soils are absorbed through the skin of the foot and engulfed by macrophages in the lower limb lymphatic system, inducing an inflammatory response in the lymphatic vessels, which results in fibrosis and obstruction of the vessel lumen.
evidence.explanation: Names lymphatic obstruction as the terminal step of the mechanism.

evidence.snippet: In 251 (86.9%) patients, both legs were affected by podoconiosis and in 38 (13.1%) only one leg was affected.
evidence.explanation: The laterality figures behind the "bilateral but not universal" claim, from a 289-patient series.

steps/13.description: Lymph cannot leave the limb. The clinical result is swelling that begins at the feet and progressively involves the legs, bilateral in about seven of eight patients, frequently asymmetric between them, and in almost all cases staying below the knee.

evidence.snippet: Increased episodes of ADLA were significantly associated with stage 3-5 podoconiosis (P = 0.002), while burning pain in the feet was more common in stage 1 or 2 podoconiosis.
evidence.explanation: Ties attack frequency to advanced stage, which is the observation behind the feedback edge - and notes that burning pain instead marks early disease.

evidence.snippet: Lymphedema can lead to skin lesions, which can serve as entry points for bacteria that may cause ADLA attacks leading to progression of the lymphedema.
evidence.explanation: States the skin-breach-to-attack-to-progression sequence, which is the loop this node closes. The source hedges it ("can", "may") and so does this entry: the edge is curated INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES.

evidence.snippet: We revealed a positive correlation between increasing lymphedema severity and non-commensal anaerobic bacteria, especially Anaerococcus provencensis, as well as a negative correlation with the presence of Corynebacterium, a constituent of normal skin flora.
evidence.explanation: Identifies what colonises the affected skin and how it tracks severity - anaerobes up, normal commensal Corynebacterium down. The correlation is with stage, so it does not establish direction on its own.

steps/14.description: Recurrent episodes of fever, pain, erythema and abrupt worsening of the swelling, precipitated by bacteria entering through fissured skin. Each episode damages the lymphatics further, so the entry models it as feeding back into the fibrotic lesion rather than as a terminal complication. It is also the outcome every trial in this disease is powered on, because it is what patients lose working days to.

evidence.snippet: The presence of microparticles of clay is demonstrated in the dermis of the foot in a patient with endemic elephantiasis. The particles are seen to be in the phagosomes of macrophages or in the cytoplasm of other cells.
evidence.explanation: Shows the particles already inside macrophage phagosomes in the foot dermis, which is the step this edge asserts.

edges/4.description: How a mineral particle comes to be presented on an HLA class II molecule is the central unsolved step in this disease, so the edge is curated with unknown intermediates rather than asserted as antigen presentation.

evidence.snippet: Intralymphatic silica provoked an immediate and intense macrophage reaction with later fibrosis both within lymph vessels and to a lesser extent within lymph nodes. Lymphography indicated that the consequent obstruction resulted more from the effects of silica on vessels than on nodes.
evidence.explanation: The intralymphatic injection experiment, which establishes that the particles alone can produce the vessel lesion and locates the effect in vessels rather than nodes.

edges/5.description: Silica delivered directly into a lymphatic provokes macrophage reaction and fibrosis in the vessel wall without requiring the adaptive arm, which is the second, HLA-independent route to the same lesion.

edges/7.description: The systemic activation is measured in blood and the lesion is in the limb lymphatics; no study connects the two directly, so the edge is curated with unknown intermediates. The direction is assumed, not shown: every cited measurement is cross-sectional case-control, and systemic activation is at least as plausibly a consequence of chronic lesional inflammation and recurrent acute attacks as a cause of them.

edges/13.description: Fissured, hyperkeratotic skin is the portal of entry for the skin flora that precipitate the acute attacks.

edges/14.description: The self-reinforcing loop. Repeated acute inflammation is held to accelerate the underlying fibrosis; the step is described consistently in the clinical literature but has not been dissected, so it is curated with unknown intermediates.

evidence.snippet: It arises due to prolonged exposure of bare feet to irritant red-clay soils in genetically susceptible individuals.
evidence.explanation: States the exposure and the susceptibility requirement together, which is exactly what this edge and its downstream HLA node jointly assert. Graded OTHER: the source is a narrative review and the sentence is its own summary statement, not a reported result.

edges/15.description: Barefoot soil contact is the route by which the mineral particles reach the skin at all; there is no other described exposure pathway.

evidence.snippet: We found a genomewide significant association of podoconiosis with the single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs17612858, located 5.8 kb from the HLA-DQA1 locus (in the allelic model: odds ratio, 2.44; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.82 to 3.26; P=1.42×10(-9); and in the additive model: odds ratio, 2.19; 95% CI, 1.66 to 2.90; P=3.44×10(-8))
evidence.explanation: The primary genome-wide association result.

evidence.snippet: HLA typing showed the alleles HLA-DRB1*0701 (odds ratio, 2.00), DQA1*0201 (odds ratio, 1.91), and DQB1*0202 (odds ratio, 1.79) and the HLA-DRB1*0701-DQB1*0202 haplotype (odds ratio, 1.92) were risk variants for podoconiosis.
evidence.explanation: The HLA-typed risk alleles and haplotype behind the SNP signal.

evidence.snippet: Fourteen SNPs in the HLA class II region showed significant genome-wide association (P < 5.0 × 10-8) with podoconiosis. The lead SNP was rs9270911 (P = 5.51 × 10-10; OR 1.53; 95% CI 1.34-1.74), located near HLA-DRB1.
evidence.explanation: Replication across three Ethiopian populations, with the lead signal shifting to HLA-DRB1.

evidence.snippet: 188 (64.1%) had a family history of podoconiosis.
evidence.explanation: Graded INDIRECT: family history in two thirds of patients is consistent with a heritable component but does not by itself separate shared genes from shared soil, since families farm the same land.

genes/0.notes: Curated as a susceptibility locus, not a causative gene. `gene_term` carries HLA-DQA1 because the slot is single-valued and the first genome-wide significant SNP sits 5.8 kb from it; the replication study's lead SNP lies near HLA-DRB1, and DQB1 is implicated by the risk haplotype. All three are bound on the pathophysiology node. Heritability is estimated at 63% and the sibling recurrence risk ratio at 5.07, so the genetic contribution is substantial - but no variant is sufficient without the soil exposure, and no locus outside HLA class II reached significance in a better-powered second genome-wide study.

evidence.snippet: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to either receive a package containing instructions for foot hygiene, skin care, bandaging, exercises, and use of socks and shoes, with support by lay Community Podoconiosis Agents at monthly meetings (intervention group)
evidence.explanation: The contents of the package, which is what this treatment describes.

evidence.snippet: The ratio of incidence rate in the intervention group to that of the control group was 0·81 (0·74 to 0·89; p<0·0001), with a rate difference of -4·5 (-5·1 to -3·8) episodes per person-year.
evidence.explanation: The effect estimate. Quoted with the absolute rates attached because the rate ratio alone hides how high the baseline burden is.

evidence.snippet: A simple, inexpensive package of lymphoedema self-care is effective in reducing the frequency and duration of acute dermatolymphangioadenitis.
evidence.explanation: The trial's own conclusion and recommendation.

evidence.snippet: There was a significant between-group difference in patients who reported any acute attacks over the study period (control n = 22 (38%), intervention n = 7 (12%), p = 0.014).
evidence.explanation: A second randomised trial, testing whether adding lymphatic stimulation to the standard package helps. It did, on acute attacks.

treatments/0.description: Foot hygiene, skin care, bandaging, exercise, elevation, and consistent use of socks and shoes, delivered through lay community agents. This is the mainstay and the only management with randomised evidence in this disease. Its measured effect is on acute attacks rather than on limb size, and the effect is real but partial - about a fifth fewer episodes, against a baseline of more than twenty per person-year.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Hygiene and emollients close the portals of bacterial entry created by fissured hyperkeratotic skin, which is the step the trial's primary outcome measures.

evidence.snippet: The DLQI values were significantly better six months after surgery than before surgery (P<0.0001).
evidence.explanation: The quality-of-life outcome at six months.

evidence.snippet: Also the number of ADLA episodes per three months was significantly lower six months after surgery than before surgery (P<0.0001).
evidence.explanation: The acute-attack reduction, which is the more surprising result: removing nodules also removed some of the infection risk.

evidence.snippet: Excisions after nodulectomy were left to heal by secondary intention with compression bandaging.
evidence.explanation: The wound-management detail that makes this a resource-appropriate procedure rather than one requiring a theatre and grafting.

treatments/1.description: Surgical excision of woody fibrotic nodules under local anaesthesia, wounds left to heal by secondary intention under compression. Reserved for nodules that do not respond to conservative care. It improves quality of life and, unexpectedly for a debulking procedure, reduces acute attack frequency.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: The procedure removes the fibrotic nodules this node produces; it does not address the lymphatic obstruction upstream of them.

evidence.snippet: Antibiotic therapy (including penicillin), which has been recommended for interruption of acute dermatolymphangioadenitis episodes,17 is not routinely available for patients in remote rural populations in Ethiopia.
evidence.explanation: Carries both halves of the claim in one sentence - the recommendation and the availability caveat. Graded OTHER: the sentence is this trial's background framing, citing an earlier recommendation, not a result of the trial itself. No trial of antibiotic therapy in podoconiosis is cited in this entry.

treatments/2.description: Antibiotics, penicillin among them, are the recommended treatment for interrupting an acute dermatolymphangioadenitis episode. Curated with the qualifier the source attaches to it and that this entry will not drop: in the remote rural populations where the disease actually occurs, they are not routinely available. The recommendation and its reach are different claims.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Antibiotics act on the bacterial arm of the acute episode, not on the lymphatic obstruction that produced the portal of entry.

evidence.snippet: Early intervention, including consistent use of footwear and improved foot hygiene, can greatly reduce disease burden.
evidence.explanation: States the effect of footwear and hygiene on disease burden. Graded OTHER because it is a review's summary statement rather than a measured result.

evidence.snippet: In stages 1 and 2, simple lymphoedema management can completely reverse the clinical changes, but if the condition is not managed with appropriate foot care and consistent shoe wearing, it can lead to subsequent ir
evidence.explanation: The reversibility claim this treatment rests on, stated for stages 1 and 2 and tied to consistent shoe wearing. Without it the description's "halt or reverse" would be asserting more than the footwear evidence shows.

evidence.snippet: Walking barefoot adjusted odd ratio (AOR) 5.35 (95% CI: 1.65, 9.05), p = 0.001, not washing feet with soap and water regularly AOR 2.8 (95% CI: 1.16, 4.44, p = 0.001), and an increased age AOR 2.23 (95% CI: 1.25, 5.58) were factors significantly associated with the prevalence of podoconiosis.
evidence.explanation: Graded INDIRECT: the odds ratio is for walking barefoot as a risk factor, so the protective effect of footwear follows by inversion rather than being measured directly. No randomised trial of footwear exists.

treatments/3.description: Shoes are the primary prevention, and in early-stage disease they are also treatment. Because the exposure is transdermal and the early lymphoedema is reversible, interrupting soil contact can halt or reverse stage 1-2 disease. This is the intervention that makes podoconiosis eliminable in a way its fellow lymphoedemas are not.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Footwear acts on the exposure itself rather than on any downstream mechanism, which is why it can prevent as well as treat.

open_questions/0.rationale: This is the hole at the centre of the disease. The exposure is known, the susceptibility locus is known and replicated, and the lesion is described in detail - but the antigen is not identified, and no mechanism connects a silicate particle to class II presentation. Kaolinite, smectite, quartz, iron oxides, beryllium and zirconium are all correlated with endemicity and none is established as causal; the systematic review that assembled them says outright that they may be covariates. Without the trigger there is no biomarker, no early diagnostic, and no target - which is why the entry's edge from particle transport to the HLA node is curated with unknown intermediates rather than as antigen presentation.

open_questions/1.rationale: The intuitive model - patients are hypersensitive to the mineral - is contradicted by the only in vitro stimulation study in this disease. Patients had higher unstimulated TNF-alpha and IL-1beta, but on stimulation the controls produced two to three times more IL-1beta. The authors read this as persistent in vivo activation, with exhaustion or regulation blunting the response to a further hit. The entry curates the result as a SUPPORT item on the immune-activation node - it supports that node's chronic-activation reading, and `supports` is relative to the record an item sits on rather than to the hypothesis the result rules out. It is curated rather than omitted because an entry that quietly dropped it would imply a hypersensitivity model the evidence does not support. It is a single small study and should not be treated as settled either way.

open_questions/2.rationale: The only experimental model in the literature injects silica directly into lymphatics, which reproduces the vessel lesion while bypassing the skin, the exposure route, the mineral species and the susceptibility genotype. There is no animal that walks barefoot on volcanic clay carrying a human class II risk haplotype, and no natural veterinary counterpart has been described. So every mechanistic claim upstream of the lymphatic vessel in this entry rests on human tissue and human genetics alone, and the one model available cannot arbitrate between the HLA-dependent and HLA-independent routes to the same lesion.

evidence.snippet: Given ongoing debate, the article proposes that trauma exposure is best defined in future iterations of the DSM and ICD as exposure to one or more psychologically threatening or horrific experiences that are overwhelming.
evidence.explanation: The diagnostic review supports traumatic exposure as the initiating context for PTSD assessment.

steps/0.description: Exposure to psychologically threatening or horrific traumatic events is the initiating environmental context required for PTSD.

evidence.snippet: We used data from individuals of European ancestry with mTBI enrolled in TRACK-TBI (n = 714), a prospective longitudinal study of level 1 trauma center patients.
evidence.explanation: Prospective trauma-center cohort data support inherited liability as a post-trauma PTSD risk modifier.

evidence.snippet: The adjusted odds of PTSD in the uppermost PTSD-PRS quintile was nearly four times higher (aOR = 3.71, 95% CI 1.80–7.65) than in the lowest PTSD-PRS quintile.
evidence.explanation: A PTSD polygenic risk score predicted probable PTSD after mild traumatic brain injury.

evidence.snippet: While not supporting a causal relationship, genetic analyses revealed a significant association between PTSD and iRBD, consistent with the exploratory imaging substudy. These findings suggest that individuals genetically at risk for PTSD may also be at higher risk for iRBD.
evidence.explanation: Genome-wide genetic analyses found a significant (explicitly non-causal) genetic association between PTSD and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, suggesting individuals genetically at risk for PTSD may also be at higher risk for iRBD.

steps/1.description: Common-variant genetic liability increases the probability of probable PTSD after traumatic injury, but does not by itself cause PTSD without a trauma context. PTSD genetic liability is also genetically correlated with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (an early synucleinopathy marker); this association is explicitly non-causal and does not establish a shared disease mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Studies show that environmental stressors can induce various epigenetic changes that shape the PTSD phenotype.
evidence.explanation: Review evidence supports environmentally induced epigenetic regulation as a PTSD susceptibility and phenotype mechanism.

evidence.snippet: This review investigated gene methylation changes in association with PTSD, including those related to the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, neurotransmitters, and immune system functioning, as well as the role of histones and regulatory noncoding RNAs.
evidence.explanation: The reviewed molecular systems map directly to HPA, neurotransmission, and immune pathophysiology nodes.

steps/2.description: Trauma and other environmental stressors are associated with epigenetic mechanisms affecting HPA-axis, neurotrophic, neurotransmitter, and immune systems relevant to PTSD.

evidence.snippet: Morning and 24 h cortisol were significantly lower in PTSD than in controls (g = -0.21; 95% CI: -0.42-(-0.01); g = -0.31; CI: -0.60-(-0.03)).
evidence.explanation: Meta-analysis supports lower cortisol measures in PTSD compared with controls.

steps/3.description: PTSD is associated with altered hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis regulation, including lower morning and 24-hour cortisol in meta-analysis, though moderator patterns are inconsistent.

evidence.snippet: some individuals with PTSD also exhibit elevated concentrations of inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor-α.
evidence.explanation: Review evidence supports inflammatory-marker elevation in a subset of individuals with PTSD.

evidence.snippet: Major findings included elevated levels of serum proinflammatory cytokines in individuals with PTSD across various trauma types, as compared with those without PTSD.
evidence.explanation: Structured review evidence supports increased proinflammatory cytokines across trauma contexts.

evidence.snippet: Recently, studies emphasized the role of inflammatory biomarkers, such as C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), as well as changes in monocyte and T-cell phenotypes, in PTSD.
evidence.explanation: Review synthesizes evidence for specific immune phenotypes (CRP/IL-6/TNF-α, monocyte/T-cell alterations) that characterize PTSD immune heterogeneity.

evidence.snippet: peripheral immune signaling, endocrine regulation, and glial-vascular interactions play a role in modulating neural circuit functions, which in turn can impact synaptic plasticity and network dynamics.
evidence.explanation: Review emphasizes the multi-scale integration of immune signaling, endocrine dysregulation (HPA axis), and glial-vascular interactions in shaping circuit-level and behavioral phenotypes in PTSD.

steps/4.description: PTSD is associated with heterogeneous peripheral immune activation characterized by elevated inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, IL-6, TNF-α) and altered monocyte/T-cell phenotypes that interface with endocrine dysregulation (HPA axis) and glial-vascular interactions to modulate neural circuit function and synaptic plasticity. Immune signaling alterations in specific immune cell phenotypes may map to distinct clinical symptom clusters (fear reactivity, hyperarousal, sleep disturbance) and disease heterogeneity.

evidence.snippet: particular brain regions may be identifiable as neural correlates of PTSD, including the prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and amygdala of the brain.
evidence.explanation: Review evidence supports amygdala-hippocampal-prefrontal circuitry as a PTSD-relevant neurobiological substrate.

steps/5.description: Altered amygdala, hippocampal, and prefrontal cortical function affects threat detection, emotional regulation, fear reactivity, and traumatic memory processing.

evidence.snippet: PTSD is characterized by nightmares, flashbacks and avoidance of stressors.
evidence.explanation: Review abstract supports nightmares and flashbacks as PTSD symptom features.

steps/6.description: Recurrent intrusive traumatic memories, flashbacks, and nightmares.

evidence.snippet: the clinical presentation of PTSDs; psychological models of PTSDs; how to approach assessment and differential diagnosis
evidence.explanation: The diagnostic review addresses the clinical presentation and assessment of PTSD generally; this quoted fragment does not itself enumerate arousal or anxiety symptoms, so it supports the phenotype only indirectly as diagnostic context.

steps/7.description: Persistent threat perception, heightened arousal, fearfulness, and anxiety.

evidence.snippet: Many patients with mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) are at risk for mental health problems such as posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
evidence.explanation: TRACK-TBI frames PTSD risk in a post-trauma cohort and tests genetic susceptibility in that context.

edges/0.description: Trauma exposure is required, while inherited liability modifies who develops persistent PTSD symptoms after exposure.

evidence.snippet: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is often associated with alterations in the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis.
evidence.explanation: Meta-analysis supports HPA-axis involvement after PTSD develops.

edges/1.description: Traumatic stress activates stress-response pathways that can become persistently dysregulated in PTSD.

edges/2.description: Genetic and environmental susceptibility are represented as upstream of molecular regulation systems involved in stress responses.

edges/3.description: Epigenetic changes in HPA-axis-related genes are modeled upstream of altered endocrine stress regulation.

edges/4.description: Epigenetic changes in immune-function genes are modeled upstream of altered inflammatory signaling.

evidence.snippet: these alterations may further reinforce the related clinical symptoms of PTSD such as sustained fear and anxiety.
evidence.explanation: The review links glucocorticoid signaling, HPA-axis function, immune function, and PTSD symptoms, but presents a proposed pathway rather than a single definitive causal experiment.

edges/5.description: Stress-hormone regulation interacts with inflammatory signaling in PTSD models and clinical studies.

evidence.snippet: Importantly, inflammation can influence neural circuits and neurotransmitter signaling in regions of the brain relevant to fear, anxiety, and emotion regulation.
evidence.explanation: This supports downstream circuit effects through immune signaling; stress-axis involvement is part of the broader PTSD biology.

edges/6.description: Stress-axis dysregulation affects limbic and prefrontal systems that regulate fear, anxiety, and memory.

evidence.snippet: neuroimaging-based studies demonstrated that altered inflammatory markers are associated with structural and functional alterations in brain regions that are responsible for the regulation of stress and emotion, including the amygdala, hippocampus, and frontal cortex.
evidence.explanation: This directly links inflammatory markers with PTSD-relevant stress/emotion brain circuitry.

edges/7.description: Inflammatory markers are associated with structural and functional alterations in amygdala, hippocampus, and frontal cortex.

evidence.snippet: Dysfunction in the regions of the prefrontal cortex, amygdala, and hippocampus are then responsible for functions of executive control, emotional lability, fear reactivity, and retrieval of traumatic memories as demonstrated in PTSD.
evidence.explanation: The review links dysfunction in these regions to traumatic-memory retrieval and fear reactivity.

edges/8.description: Abnormal threat and memory circuitry contributes to intrusive traumatic recollections and flashbacks.

edges/9.description: Altered threat circuitry contributes to persistent threat perception, hyperarousal, and anxiety.

evidence.snippet: Evidence supports efficacy of exposure therapy (high SOE) including the manualized version Prolonged Exposure (PE); cognitive therapy (CT), cognitive processing therapy (CPT), cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)-mixed therapies (moderate SOE); eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) and narrative exposure therapy (low-moderate SOE).
evidence.explanation: Systematic review evidence supports trauma-focused psychotherapy options including PE, CPT, CBT-based therapies, EMDR, and narrative exposure therapy for adults with PTSD.

evidence.snippet: This randomized clinical trial found that although PE was statistically more effective than CPT, the difference was not clinically significant, and improvements in PTSD were meaningful in both treatment groups.
evidence.explanation: A large randomized trial supports both prolonged exposure and cognitive processing therapy as effective PTSD psychotherapies.

treatments/0.description: First-line trauma-focused psychotherapies for PTSD include exposure therapy such as prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy, EMDR, and narrative exposure therapy.

evidence.snippet: For individual monotherapy agents compared to placebo in two or more studies, we found small statistically significant evidence for the antidepressants fluoxetine, paroxetine, sertraline, venlafaxine and the antipsychotic quetiapine.
evidence.explanation: Systematic review and meta-analysis evidence supports several antidepressant monotherapies for reducing PTSD symptom severity, including paroxetine, sertraline, and venlafaxine.

treatments/1.description: SSRI and SNRI pharmacotherapy can be used for PTSD symptom reduction, including sertraline, paroxetine, and venlafaxine.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: SSRIs/SNRIs raise serotonergic (and noradrenergic) tone in the amygdala-prefrontal-hippocampal threat circuitry, facilitating fear extinction and reducing hyperarousal and re-experiencing symptoms.

evidence.snippet: But all, even when resistant to conventional treatment (TR), respond quickly to low dose (0.5-1.0 mg/kg I.M.) ketamine.
evidence.explanation: Recorded as PARTIAL rather than SUPPORT because this statement appears in the paper's Background and summarizes prior literature on ketamine responsiveness across treatment-resistant neurotic disorders. It is not a primary efficacy finding of this study, which was a mechanistic EEG study without an efficacy endpoint. It is cited here to document ketamine as an investigational PTSD option, not to assert established efficacy.

treatments/2.description: Low-dose intramuscular ketamine is an investigational, off-label rapid-acting treatment explored for treatment-resistant PTSD. It is not an approved PTSD indication. Unlike the intravenous and intranasal esketamine routes used in treatment-resistant depression, the PTSD literature cited here uses intramuscular dosing at 0.5-1.0 mg/kg.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Ketamine acts on glutamatergic signaling within the amygdala-prefrontal-hippocampal threat circuitry. Resting frontal EEG power changes following dosing are proposed to index this modulation in treatment-resistant PTSD, though the causal link remains unestablished.

evidence.snippet: TR-PTSD patients showed dose- and band frequency-dependent EEG power changes (particularly alpha at 0.05 mg/kg), while TR-MDD patients did not.
evidence.explanation: Primary result distinguishing the ketamine EEG response of treatment-resistant PTSD from that of treatment-resistant major depression. Note that the dose quoted in this Results sentence (0.05 mg/kg) is inconsistent with the Methods, which specify 0.5 or 1.0 mg/kg I.M. The snippet is reproduced verbatim from the abstract; the discrepancy appears to be an error in the source publication and should not be propagated as a dosing claim.

evidence.snippet: Ketamine effects and their therapeutic links vary in band and site with DSM diagnosis - including previous TR anxiety results.
evidence.explanation: Authors' conclusion that ketamine's neural and therapeutic effects are diagnosis-specific, motivating a disorder-specific rather than shared mechanism across treatment-resistant neurotic disorders.

hypotheses/0.description: Resting frontal EEG power changes following low-dose intramuscular ketamine are proposed to index a disorder-specific neural system in treatment-resistant PTSD, distinguishing it from treatment-resistant major depression. In a small controlled study using fentanyl as an active comparator, TR-PTSD patients showed dose- and band-dependent EEG power changes, notably in the alpha band, while TR-MDD patients did not; power change correlated with symptom-scale change at differing bands and electrodes across diagnoses. The authors interpret this as evidence that ketamine engages the disorder-specific systems that conventional treatments target. The hypothesis rests on a single study of 22 TR-PTSD patients (20F, 2M), is not yet independently replicated, and the direction of causality between EEG change and symptom change is unresolved.

evidence.snippet: Only three enzymes (PDSS1, PDSS2 and COQ2) are required for assembly and attachment of the polyisoprenoid side chain.
evidence.explanation: Defines the three genes that act at this segment of the pathway, which is the gene set bound on this node.

evidence.snippet: The PDSS1 gene encodes prenyl diphosphate synthase subunit 1, an enzyme that supplies decaprenyl diphosphate, the precursor for the side chain of the isoprenoid quinone Coenzyme Q10 that functions as a mobile electron carrier in the respiratory chain, as well as other mitochondrial functions including antioxidant properties.
evidence.explanation: Names the decaprenyl diphosphate synthase activity bound on this node and its role in supplying the CoQ10 side chain.

evidence.snippet: In the second family, direct sequencing of OH-benzoate polyprenyltransferase (COQ2), the human ortholog of the yeast COQ2 gene, identified a single base pair frameshift deletion resulting in a premature stop codon (c.1198delT, N401fsX415).
evidence.explanation: Names the 4-hydroxybenzoate polyprenyltransferase activity bound on this node, and the biallelic COQ2 defect that abolishes it.

evidence.snippet: The visual system seems to be mainly involved when the first steps of CoQ10 synthesis are impaired (PDSS1, PDSS2, and COQ2 deficiency).
evidence.explanation: Groups PDSS1, PDSS2 and COQ2 as the first-step enzymes and reports the phenotypic emphasis this node's description records.

steps/10.description: The first steps of CoQ10 biosynthesis build the polyisoprenoid tail and attach it to the 4-hydroxybenzoate ring. Only three of the disease genes act here: PDSS1 and PDSS2 each encode a subunit of the decaprenyl diphosphate synthase that supplies the side chain, and COQ2 is the polyprenyltransferase that joins it to the ring. Biallelic defects in this segment therefore block CoQ10 assembly at its earliest committed step, and the reported phenotypes of this segment include prominent visual involvement.

evidence.snippet: The majority of these enzymes are responsible for modifications of the CoQ-head group (benzoquinone ring).
evidence.explanation: Establishes head-group modification as the segment most of the CoQ10 biosynthesis enzymes act in.

evidence.snippet: The head-modifying enzymes may assemble into resolvable domains, representing COQ complexes.
evidence.explanation: Source for describing this segment's enzymes as assembling into COQ complexes.

evidence.snippet: Biallelic pathogenic variants in COQ7, encoding mitochondrial 5-demethoxyubiquinone hydroxylase, have been reported in nine patients from seven families.
evidence.explanation: Names the demethoxyubiquinone hydroxylase activity bound on this node and the gene that carries it.

evidence.snippet: The COQ5 gene encodes coenzyme Q5, methyltransferase which is involved in mitochondrial ubiquinone (coenzyme Q10, CoQ10) biosynthesis.
evidence.explanation: Places COQ5's methyltransferase activity in this segment.

evidence.snippet: The conserved COQ9 residues necessary for its interaction with COQ7 comprise a surface patch around the lipid-binding site, suggesting that COQ9 might serve to present its bound lipid to COQ7.
evidence.explanation: Structural and mass-spectrometry work placing COQ9 as COQ7's lipid-binding partner within this segment.

steps/11.description: Most of the CoQ10 biosynthesis enzymes act after side-chain attachment, on the benzoquinone ring, and may assemble into resolvable domains described as COQ complexes. COQ4, COQ5, COQ6, COQ7 and COQ9 act in this segment: COQ5 is the pathway's methyltransferase, COQ6 its monooxygenase, COQ7 the demethoxyubiquinone hydroxylase, and COQ9 a lipid-binding protein that presents its bound lipid to COQ7. Biallelic defects in this segment therefore block CoQ10 maturation after the side chain has been attached.

evidence.snippet: The COQ8B gene encodes the COQ8B protein, which is an atypical kinase that is expressed in the podocytes of the kidney and localizes to the mitochondrial matrix, where it participates in coenzyme Q10 synthesis.
evidence.explanation: Source for describing COQ8B as an atypical kinase participating in CoQ10 synthesis, and for the podocyte cell type bound on this node.

evidence.snippet: In human podocytes, ADCK4 interacted with members of the CoQ10 biosynthesis pathway, including COQ6, which has been linked with SRNS and COQ7.
evidence.explanation: Shows COQ8B, then named ADCK4, physically associating with head-group enzymes of the pathway in human podocytes.

evidence.snippet: ADCK4 was highly similar to ADCK3, which has been shown to participate in coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) biosynthesis.
evidence.explanation: Records COQ8A, then named ADCK3, as an already established participant in CoQ10 biosynthesis, and as the paralogue by whose similarity COQ8B was recognised.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in ADCK4 resulted in reduced CoQ10 levels and reduced mitochondrial respiratory enzyme activity in cells isolated from individuals with SRNS and transformed lymphoblasts.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived cells carrying biallelic COQ8B variants show the reduced CoQ10 this node's defect produces.

steps/12.description: COQ8A and COQ8B are closely similar atypical kinases that support the CoQ10 biosynthetic machinery rather than being assigned a named chemical step of the pathway. COQ8B localises to the mitochondrial matrix of kidney podocytes and interacts with pathway members including COQ6 and COQ7, and COQ8A was established as a pathway participant before COQ8B was identified. Loss of COQ8B reduces cellular CoQ10 in patient-derived cells.

evidence.snippet: In man, at least 10 genes are required for the biosynthesis of functional CoQ10, a mutation in any one of which can result in a deficit in CoQ10 status.
evidence.explanation: Defects in any of the CoQ10 biosynthesis genes reduce functional CoQ10, the shared upstream defect.

steps/13.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants in any of the nuclear CoQ10 biosynthesis genes (PDSS1, PDSS2, COQ2, COQ4, COQ5, COQ6, COQ7, COQ8A, COQ8B, COQ9) reduce endogenous CoQ10 production, lowering tissue and cellular CoQ10 levels. This is the shared upstream lesion across all primary CoQ10 deficiency subtypes.

evidence.snippet: Coenzyme Q(10) (CoQ(10)) is a vital lipophilic molecule that transfers electrons from mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I and II to complex III.
evidence.explanation: CoQ10 transfers electrons from complexes I and II to complex III; its deficiency impairs respiratory electron transport.

steps/14.description: CoQ10 normally shuttles electrons from respiratory chain complexes I and II to complex III. Reduced CoQ10 impairs this electron transfer, decreasing oxidative phosphorylation and ATP synthesis, biochemically detectable as reduced combined complex I+III and II+III activities.

evidence.snippet: CoQ10 deficiency exerts detrimental effects on the nervous system. Potential consequences are neuronal death, neuroinflammation and cerebral gliosis.
evidence.explanation: CoQ10 deficiency causes neuronal death, neuroinflammation, and gliosis as downstream tissue injury.

evidence.snippet: However, there are many other cellular pathways that also depend on the CoQ10 supply (redox homeostasis, ferroptosis and sulfide oxidation).
evidence.explanation: Non-bioenergetic CoQ10-dependent pathways (redox homeostasis, ferroptosis defense, sulfide oxidation) are also disrupted.

steps/15.description: Beyond bioenergetics, CoQ10 is a lipid-soluble antioxidant and supports redox homeostasis, ferroptosis defense, and sulfide oxidation. Combined energy failure and loss of antioxidant/redox protection produce multisystem injury, with the nervous system, kidney, heart, and sensory organs particularly vulnerable. Neurologic injury involves neuronal death, neuroinflammation, and cerebral gliosis.

evidence.snippet: Clinical features include encephalopathy, regression, movement disorders, epilepsy and intellectual disability.
evidence.explanation: Encephalopathy is a recognized core neurologic feature of CoQ10 deficiency.

steps/16.description: Encephalopathy with developmental delay/regression is a core neurologic manifestation, especially in neonatal/infantile-onset forms.

evidence.snippet: Clinical features include encephalopathy, regression, movement disorders, epilepsy and intellectual disability.
evidence.explanation: Epilepsy/seizures are recognized neurologic features.

steps/17.description: Epilepsy/seizures are common, particularly in severe early-onset forms.

evidence.snippet: Each mutation was linked to early-onset SRNS with sensorineural deafness.
evidence.explanation: Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome is a key renal manifestation, shown here for COQ6.

steps/18.description: Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome is a major renal manifestation in COQ2, COQ6, and COQ8B forms and can progress to end-stage kidney disease.

edges/20.description: Failure to assemble or attach the polyisoprenoid side chain blocks CoQ10 production at the earliest committed step.

edges/21.description: Failure to complete benzoquinone ring modification leaves CoQ10 unfinished and reduces mature CoQ10.

edges/22.description: Loss of COQ8 kinase support of the biosynthetic machinery reduces cellular CoQ10.

edges/23.description: Reduced CoQ10 impairs electron transfer in the respiratory chain.

edges/24.description: Energy failure combined with loss of CoQ10 antioxidant and redox functions drives multisystem injury.

evidence.snippet: Clinical features include encephalopathy, regression, movement disorders, epilepsy and intellectual disability.
evidence.explanation: Names encephalopathy as a clinical consequence of the nervous-system injury this node describes.

edges/25.description: Neuronal death, neuroinflammation and gliosis in the CoQ10-deficient nervous system present clinically as encephalopathy.

evidence.snippet: Clinical features include encephalopathy, regression, movement disorders, epilepsy and intellectual disability.
evidence.explanation: Names epilepsy as a clinical consequence of the nervous-system injury this node describes.

edges/26.description: The same neuronal injury produces epilepsy, which in the severe early-onset forms is often refractory.

evidence.snippet: Knockdown of adck4 in zebrafish and Drosophila recapitulated nephrotic syndrome-associated phenotypes.
evidence.explanation: Loss of a CoQ10 biosynthesis gene reproduces nephrotic syndrome in two animal models, supporting the mechanism-to-phenotype step.

evidence.snippet: We also demonstrate that early diagnosis and treatment of CoQ10 deficiency with oral supplementation (30 mg/kg/d) can reverse renal manifestations and can completely prevent kidney disease over 10 years of follow-up.
evidence.explanation: Restoring CoQ10 reverses and prevents the renal disease in patients, which supports the edge by therapeutic response rather than by direct observation of the intervening steps.

edges/27.description: Podocytes are among the cell types that fail under CoQ10 deficiency, and that failure presents as steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Transformation of yeast Deltacoq1 and Deltacoq2 strains by mutant yeast COQ1 and mutant human COQ2 genes, respectively, resulted in defective growth on respiratory medium, indicating that these mutations are indeed the cause of OXPHOS deficiency.
evidence.explanation: Yeast complementation establishes the patients' COQ2 and PDSS1/COQ1 alleles as loss-of-function and as the cause of the OXPHOS defect.

genes/0.notes: COQ2 (HGNC-approved name "coenzyme Q2, polyprenyltransferase", 4q21.23) acts at the side-chain attachment step, joining the polyisoprenoid tail to 4-hydroxybenzoate. The gene-specific allelic series, genotype-phenotype relationship and the separate multiple-system-atrophy susceptibility question are curated in COQ2-Related_Primary_Coenzyme_Q10_Deficiency.

evidence.snippet: We identified five recessive missense mutations in COQ4 segregating with disease in all four families.
evidence.explanation: Recessive COQ4 missense alleles segregating with disease across four families.

evidence.snippet: The early mortality in our cohort suggests that COQ4 is an essential component of the multisubunit complex required for CoQ(10) biosynthesis.
evidence.explanation: Source for describing COQ4 as a component of the biosynthetic complex rather than a catalytic step.

genes/1.notes: COQ4 (9q34.11) is described by the cohort below as an essential component of the multisubunit CoQ10 biosynthetic complex, which its authors read as consistent with the uniformly severe neonatal phenotype. The gene-specific cohort is curated in COQ4-Related_Neonatal_Encephalomyopathy.

evidence.snippet: Three variants (1 large tandem duplication, 1 canonical splice-site, 1 missense) that have been reported in 2 probands in 2 publications (PMIDs: 29044765, 37599337) are included in this curation. The mechanism of pathogenicity appears to be loss of function.
evidence.explanation: ClinGen's summary of the COQ5 allelic evidence and of the loss-of-function mechanism, and the basis for the Moderate grade recorded in the notes.

genes/2.notes: COQ5 (HGNC-approved name "coenzyme Q5, methyltransferase", 12q24.31) is the pathway's methyltransferase. The evidence base is two probands, which is why ClinGen's grade is Moderate; a large tandem duplication, a canonical splice-site variant and a missense variant are the reported alleles.

evidence.snippet: Here we have identified 6 different mutations in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis monooxygenase 6 (COQ6) in 13 individuals from 7 families by homozygosity mapping.
evidence.explanation: Thirteen individuals from seven families carrying biallelic COQ6 variants.

evidence.snippet: The deleterious effects of these human COQ6 mutations were validated by their lack of complementation in coq6-deficient yeast.
evidence.explanation: Yeast complementation establishes the patient alleles as loss of function.

genes/3.notes: COQ6 (HGNC-approved name "coenzyme Q6, monooxygenase", 14q24.3) is the pathway's monooxygenase, acting on the benzoquinone ring. The gene-specific cohort and the oto-renal phenotype are curated in COQ6-Related_Steroid-Resistant_Nephrotic_Syndrome.

evidence.snippet: ADCK4 was highly similar to ADCK3, which has been shown to participate in coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) biosynthesis.
evidence.explanation: Records COQ8A, under its previous symbol ADCK3, as an established participant in CoQ10 biosynthesis.

genes/4.notes: COQ8A (1q42.13) is the paralogue of COQ8B and, like it, supports the biosynthetic machinery rather than being assigned a catalytic step of the pathway. HGNC records ADCK3 and CABC1 as previous symbols for this gene. The cerebellar-ataxia phenotype is curated in Autosomal_Recessive_Ataxia_Due_to_Ubiquinone_Deficiency. ClinGen has no assertion for this gene: grepping the committed cache/clingen/gene_validity.csv for COQ8A, ADCK3, CABC1 and HGNC:16812 returns no row.

evidence.snippet: While various names have been given to the constellation of features seen in those with COQ8B -related disease, pathogenic variants in this gene cause a primary mitochondrial disease.
evidence.explanation: ClinGen's statement that the COQ8B presentations are one disease entity, which is the lumping decision recorded in the notes.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, a patient with SRNS with a homozygous ADCK4 frameshift mutation had partial remission following CoQ10 treatment.
evidence.explanation: A biallelic COQ8B patient whose renal disease partially remitted on CoQ10, supporting a causative and treatable relationship.

genes/5.notes: COQ8B (19q13.2) is the COQ8A paralogue, expressed in kidney podocytes. HGNC records ADCK4 as its previous symbol. ClinGen lumps the COQ8B renal and mitochondrial presentations into a single disease entity, whereas MONDO keeps the renal concept as nephrotic syndrome type 9 under familial idiopathic steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Overall, we define two distinct disease presentations of COQ7-related disorder with emerging genotype-phenotype correlation and validate the use of the yeast model for functional studies of COQ7 variants.
evidence.explanation: The authors' conclusion that COQ7 produces two distinct presentations with a genotype-phenotype correlation.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that the coenzyme Q analogue 2,4-dihydroxybensoic acid (2,4DHB) was able to specifically bypass the COQ7 deficiency, increase cellular coenzyme Q levels and rescue the biochemical defect in patient fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Bypassing the COQ7 step in patient fibroblasts restores CoQ, which locates the defect at that enzymatic step.

genes/6.notes: COQ7 (HGNC-approved name "coenzyme Q7, hydroxylase", 16p12.3) hydroxylates demethoxyubiquinone. The report below delineates two presentations with an emerging genotype-phenotype correlation and validates a yeast assay for COQ7 variants. ClinGen has no assertion for this gene: grepping the committed cache/clingen/gene_validity.csv for COQ7 and for HGNC:2244 returns no row.

evidence.snippet: Site-directed mutagenesis targeting the equivalent residue in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae abolished respiratory growth.
evidence.explanation: Functional confirmation that the truncating COQ9 allele abolishes respiratory competence.

evidence.snippet: Cultured skin fibroblasts from the patient had a coenzyme Q(10) biosynthetic rate of 11% of normal controls and accumulated an abnormal metabolite that we believe to be a biosynthetic intermediate.
evidence.explanation: Patient fibroblasts show a residual CoQ10 biosynthetic rate of 11% of controls together with an accumulated upstream intermediate.

genes/7.notes: COQ9 (16q21) is a lipid-binding protein that partners COQ7; HGNC records C16orf49 as its previous symbol. ClinGen carries two assertions for this gene, Definitive against mitochondrial disease and Limited against Leigh syndrome specifically, so the Definitive grade should not be read as a Leigh-syndrome claim.

evidence.snippet: A genome-wide search for homozygosity in family 1 identified a region of chromosome 10 encompassing the gene prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1), which encodes the human ortholog of the yeast COQ1 gene, a key enzyme of CoQ10 synthesis.
evidence.explanation: Maps the first PDSS1 family to chromosome 10 and identifies the gene as the human COQ1 orthologue.

genes/8.notes: PDSS1 (HGNC-approved name "decaprenyl diphosphate synthase subunit 1", 10p12.1) is the human orthologue of yeast COQ1 and supplies the decaprenyl diphosphate side chain; HGNC records TPRT as its previous symbol. The committed ClinGen record grades it Moderate and names PDSS1-related primary mitochondrial disease as its single disease entity.

evidence.snippet: Biochemical assays with radiolabeled substrates indicated a severe defect in decaprenyl diphosphate synthase in the patient's fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Direct enzymatic confirmation that the biallelic PDSS2 variants impair decaprenyl diphosphate synthase activity.

evidence.snippet: This is the first description of pathogenic mutations in PDSS2 and confirms the molecular and clinical heterogeneity of primary CoQ(10) deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The first reported PDSS2 patient, presented by the authors as evidence of the genetic heterogeneity of primary CoQ10 deficiency.

genes/9.notes: PDSS2 (HGNC-approved name "decaprenyl diphosphate synthase subunit 2", 6q21) is the second subunit of the same side-chain synthase; HGNC records C6orf210 as its previous symbol. The committed cache/clingen/gene_validity.csv holds a single PDSS2 row, filed against Leigh syndrome at Moderate rather than against a numbered CoQ10 deficiency class.

evidence.snippet: We also demonstrate that early diagnosis and treatment of CoQ10 deficiency with oral supplementation (30 mg/kg/d) can reverse renal manifestations and can completely prevent kidney disease over 10 years of follow-up.
evidence.explanation: Early high-dose oral CoQ10 can reverse and prevent renal disease.

evidence.snippet: We show that oral doses of CoQ10 up to 70 mg/kg/d were needed to ameliorate neurologic features.
evidence.explanation: Higher doses (up to 70 mg/kg/day) were required to ameliorate neurologic features.

treatments/0.description: High-dose oral CoQ10 (ubiquinone/ubiquinol) supplementation is the only disease-directed therapy. Early treatment can reverse or prevent renal disease (around 30 mg/kg/day) and ameliorate neurologic features (up to 70 mg/kg/day); benefit is limited once irreversible organ injury is established, and severe neonatal forms often respond poorly.

evidence.snippet: Additional idebenone was required to control seizures in some cases, and 3 children with neonatal-onset neurologic disease died in early childhood despite receiving high-dose oral CoQ10 from birth.
evidence.explanation: Idebenone was used as an adjunct to control seizures in some patients.

treatments/1.description: Idebenone, a synthetic CoQ10 analogue, was used as an adjunct to control seizures in some patients (10-20 mg/kg/day).

evidence.snippet: definitive proof that PH Type 3 is due to deficiency of the
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates via loss-of-function nonsense variants that PH3 results from deficiency of the 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase enzyme.

evidence.snippet: HOGA1 is a mitochondrial
evidence.explanation: Establishes HOGA1 as the mitochondrial 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase acting in the hydroxyproline pathway.

evidence.snippet: aldolase, catalyzing the final step in the metabolic pathway of hydroxyproline.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the HOGA1 gene product as the aldolase catalyzing the final step of hydroxyproline metabolism.

steps/1.description: Biallelic loss-of-function HOGA1 variants abolish mitochondrial 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase activity, the fourth and final enzymatic step of the hepatic hydroxyproline degradation pathway that cleaves 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate into pyruvate and glyoxylate.

The precise pathomechanism remains uncertain.
